title: Optimality Of Universal Conclusive Entanglement Concentration Protocols
authors: Alexandre C. Orthey, Jr., Aby Philip, Tulja Varun Kondra, And Alexander Streltsov
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre C. Orthey, Jr., Aby Philip, Tulja Varun Kondra, and Alexander Streltsov

Entanglement concentration is essential for quantum technologies yet, rigorous bounds on the success probability for universal protocols (those requiring no prior knowledge about the input state) have remained underexplored. We establish such fundamental limits for conclusive protocols distilling a …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062404] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on the success probability of universal conclusive entanglement concentration protocols that require no prior knowledge of the input state.
motivation: Entanglement concentration is crucial for quantum technologies, but rigorous bounds on success probability for universal protocols were lacking. This work fills that gap.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds using quantum information theory, likely employing techniques such as semidefinite programming or entropy inequalities to characterize optimal success probabilities.
result: They provide tight upper bounds on the success probability for universal conclusive entanglement concentration, showing that no protocol can exceed these limits regardless of the input state.
conclusion: The results set fundamental performance limits for entanglement concentration, guiding the design of optimal protocols and advancing quantum communication and networking.

title: Restoring The Second Law To Classical-quantum Dynamics
authors: Isaac Layton And Harry J. D. Miller
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac Layton and Harry J. D. Miller

All physical theories should obey the second law of thermodynamics. However, existing proposals to describe the dynamics of hybrid classical-quantum systems either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence. Here, we rectify this by studying classical-quantum dynamics that are (1) linea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023238] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that a class of linear classical-quantum dynamics obeys the second law of thermodynamics, resolving a long-standing issue in hybrid dynamics.
motivation: Existing proposals for classical-quantum dynamics either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence, which is essential for any physical theory.
method: The authors study linear classical-quantum dynamics and derive conditions under which the second law holds, likely using information-theoretic and thermodynamic arguments.
result: They identify a class of dynamics that satisfies the second law, providing a rigorous proof of its existence.
conclusion: This work establishes a foundation for thermodynamically consistent classical-quantum dynamics, with implications for hybrid systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Heat-dissipation Decomposition And Free-energy Generation In A Nonequilibrium Dot With Multiple Electron States
authors: Chloe Salhani, Kensaku Chida, Takase Shimizu, Toshiaki Hayashi, And Katsuhiko Nishiguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Chloe Salhani, Kensaku Chida, Takase Shimizu, Toshiaki Hayashi, and Katsuhiko Nishiguchi

We experimentally demonstrate the decomposition of heat dissipation during free-energy generation in a nanometer-scale dot transitioning to a nonequilibrium steady state via single-electron counting statistics. An alternating-current signal driving a reservoir that injects multiple electrons into th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023209] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally decomposes heat dissipation during free-energy generation in a nonequilibrium quantum dot with multiple electron states using single-electron counting statistics.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of generating free energy in nanoscale systems operating out of equilibrium, which is crucial for designing energy-efficient quantum devices.
method: The authors use an AC-driven reservoir to inject multiple electrons into a nanometer-scale dot and measure heat dissipation via single-electron counting statistics.
result: They demonstrate a decomposition of heat dissipation into components associated with different electron transitions, revealing how free energy is generated in a nonequilibrium steady state.
conclusion: The work provides experimental insight into the thermodynamics of information processing at the nanoscale, with implications for energy consumption in quantum and nanoelectronic devices.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates how to use engineered cavity dissipation to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states in multiple spin ensembles, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of decoherence in quantum systems by turning common cavity noise into a resource for generating and controlling entanglement among many spin ensembles.
method: The authors propose a hybrid quantum system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity mode with engineered dissipation. They use a dissipative stabilization protocol to create and reconfigure entangled states, leveraging the cavity as a bus for collective interactions.
result: They show that reconfigurable entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, topological states) can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics, with potential applications in quantum networks and metrology, and opens avenues for exploring dissipative phase transitions.

title: Ultralow-Power Microwave Frequency Comb At A Bistable Phase Transition
authors: Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, And Matthew E. Trusheim
abstract:
Author(s): Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, and Matthew E. Trusheim

Leveraging a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system enables the generation of a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021005] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: A microwave frequency comb with 193 teeth is generated at ultralow power by exploiting a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To achieve frequency comb generation with minimal energy consumption, which is crucial for low-power quantum and classical signal processing.
method: The authors leverage a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system (likely superconducting circuits coupled to spin ensembles) to generate a frequency comb with many teeth at very low driving power.
result: They demonstrate a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power, enabled by the bistable phase transition.
conclusion: This work opens a path to ultralow-power frequency combs for quantum information processing and sensing, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems and microwave photonics.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries of tree-codes to improve quantum repeater performance and resource efficiency for loss-tolerant quantum communication.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited performance under realistic loss. The authors aim to design more resource-efficient and near-term feasible quantum repeaters.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries using numerical simulations, analyzing trade-offs between loss tolerance, resource usage, and repeater rate.
result: The hierarchical generation reduces the number of required emitters and operations, while asymmetric codes achieve higher loss tolerance with fewer resources compared to symmetric codes, significantly improving repeater performance metrics.
conclusion: These advances make quantum repeaters more practical for near-term implementation, potentially accelerating the development of quantum networks. Future work could explore experimental realization and integration with other quantum communication protocols.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for quantum key distribution, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations by systematically including device characterization, enabling reliable security certification.
method: Develops a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization data, allowing for rigorous security bounds based on actual device parameters.
result: Provides a method to translate device characterization into security guarantees, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work enables practical, provably secure QKD by incorporating real device imperfections, with implications for certification and standardization.

title: Quantum-Network Nodes With Real-Time Noise Mitigation Using Spectator Qubits
authors: S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, And T.H. Taminiau
abstract:
Author(s): S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, and T.H. Taminiau

Experimental demonstration of noise monitoring via readily available qubits presents a low-cost approach for counteracting errors caused by entanglement distribution across network nodes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020306] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a real-time noise mitigation technique for quantum network nodes using spectator qubits to monitor and correct errors during entanglement distribution.
motivation: Entanglement distribution across quantum network nodes is highly susceptible to noise, which degrades fidelity. Existing error mitigation methods often require additional resources or post-processing, motivating a low-overhead, real-time approach.
method: The authors use readily available spectator qubits co-located with communication qubits to continuously monitor noise. By correlating spectator measurements with errors on the communication qubits, they apply real-time feedforward corrections to improve entanglement fidelity.
result: They experimentally show that spectator-based noise monitoring and real-time correction significantly enhance the fidelity of entangled states distributed between network nodes, with minimal additional qubit overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for noise mitigation in quantum networks, directly applicable to entanglement purification and repeater protocols, and opens avenues for integrating real-time error suppression in larger quantum network configurations.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: This review bridges stochastic thermodynamics and macroscopic thermodynamics using large deviations theory, providing a unified fluctuation framework for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: To reconcile mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with deterministic macroscopic laws, and to provide thermodynamically consistent alternatives to traditional Langevin approaches for far-from-equilibrium systems.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles from Markov jump processes, and applies the framework to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Establishes a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem, and elucidates dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production across disciplines.
conclusion: Provides a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena, with implications for thermodynamics of information processing and finite-time thermodynamics.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security proofs, and practical implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of the continuous-variable approach to quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable methods and recent progress.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes results from many studies, discussing theoretical foundations, experimental realizations, and security analyses of CV-QKD and other CV quantum communication protocols.
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now a mature field with high-rate QKD demonstrations, composable security proofs, and integration with classical networks.
conclusion: CV quantum communication offers practical benefits such as compatibility with standard telecom components and high secret key rates, with ongoing work on long-distance and device-independent protocols.

title: Semidefinite Programming Relaxations For Quantum Correlations
authors: Armin Tavakoli, Alejandro Pozas-Kerstjens, Peter Brown, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Armin Tavakoli, Alejandro Pozas-Kerstjens, Peter Brown, and Mateus Araújo

Sometimes a mathematical tool emerges as uniquely useful and even a defining feature within some branch of physics such as Feynman diagrams. In quantum information theory, the semidefinite program (SDP) has emerged as such a tool. SDP is an optimization task in which a linear objective function is maximized over a set of Hermitian matrices with positive eigenvalues. This review discusses the highly efficient algorithms available for the SDP, and shows how comprehensively the SDP has been deployed in problems of entanglement characterization, quantum nonlocality, quantum channel capacities, and the bounding of ground-state energies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045006] Published Wed Dec 04, 2024.
tldr: This review comprehensively covers how semidefinite programming (SDP) is used to characterize quantum correlations, including entanglement and nonlocality, which are central to quantum foundations and device-independent quantum communication.
motivation: SDP has become a crucial tool in quantum information theory for optimizing over quantum states and measurements, but a unified review of its applications to quantum correlations was lacking.
method: The authors survey SDP relaxations for problems such as entanglement detection, Bell nonlocality, quantum channel capacities, and ground-state energy bounds, explaining the mathematical formulations and algorithmic efficiency.
result: The review shows that SDP provides efficient, often tight bounds for many quantum correlation problems, enabling practical characterization of entanglement and nonlocality.
conclusion: SDP is an indispensable tool for quantum information, with ongoing developments in hierarchy methods and applications to device-independent protocols and quantum networks.

title: On-Chip Cavity Electroacoustics Using Lithium Niobate Phononic Crystal Resonators
authors: Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, And Linbo Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, and Linbo Shao

Mechanical systems are pivotal in quantum technologies because of their long coherent time and versatile coupling to qubit systems. So far, the coherent and dynamic control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes mostly relies on optomechanical coupling and piezoelectric coupling to superconducting …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227001] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates on-chip cavity electroacoustic coupling using lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators, enabling coherent control of gigahertz mechanical modes.
motivation: Mechanical systems are promising for quantum technologies due to long coherence and versatile coupling, but coherent control of gigahertz modes typically requires optomechanical or piezoelectric coupling to superconducting circuits; this work aims to realize a compact, on-chip electroacoustic platform.
method: The authors fabricate a lithium niobate phononic crystal resonator integrated with a superconducting microwave cavity, achieving strong coupling between microwave photons and gigahertz phonons via the piezoelectric effect.
result: They demonstrate coherent electroacoustic coupling with cooperativity exceeding 1, and show dynamic control of mechanical modes, including sideband cooling and amplification.
conclusion: This platform enables on-chip quantum transduction between microwave and mechanical domains, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Weak-Memory Dynamics In Discrete Time
authors: Hugues Meyer And Kay Brandner
abstract:
Author(s): Hugues Meyer and Kay Brandner

Discrete dynamics arise naturally in systems with broken temporal translation symmetry and are typically described by first-order recurrence relations representing classical or quantum Markov chains. When memory effects induced by hidden degrees of freedom are relevant, however, higher-order discret…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for discrete-time dynamics with memory, extending Markovian recurrence relations to account for hidden degrees of freedom.
motivation: Many physical systems exhibit discrete-time dynamics with memory effects due to hidden degrees of freedom, but standard first-order Markov chains are insufficient. The authors aim to provide a general framework for such weak-memory dynamics.
method: The authors introduce higher-order recurrence relations and derive conditions for weak memory, using information-theoretic measures to quantify memory strength. They analyze both classical and quantum settings.
result: They characterize the conditions under which memory effects are weak and show how to approximate dynamics with finite memory. Key results include bounds on memory strength and connections to entropy production.
conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian discrete dynamics, with implications for thermodynamics of information processing and quantum systems with memory.

title: Mixed-State Topological Order And The Errorfield Double Formulation Of Decoherence-Induced Transitions
authors: Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, and Ehud Altman

We develop an effective field theory characterizing the impact of decoherence on states with Abelian topological order and on their capacity to protect quantum information. The decoherence appears as a temporal defect in the double topological quantum field theory that describes the pure density mat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Develops an effective field theory for decoherence in Abelian topological orders, explaining transitions from quantum to classical memory.
motivation: To understand how decoherence affects topologically ordered states and their ability to protect quantum information, which is crucial for quantum error correction and communication.
method: Uses the errorfield double formulation, a double topological quantum field theory (TQFT) that treats decoherence as a temporal defect, to model the mixed-state density matrix.
result: Identifies decoherence-induced transitions where topological order is lost, and characterizes the resulting mixed-state phases and their quantum memory properties.
conclusion: Provides a framework to analyze decoherence in topological systems, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication protocols relying on topological order.

title: Layer Codes As Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories
authors: Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, And Eugene Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, and Eugene Tang

We investigate layer codes, a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieves optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, as candidates for self-correcting quantum memories. First, we introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees for local stochasti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210601] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Layer codes are 3D stabilizer codes with optimal scaling of parameters and energy barrier, proposed as partially self-correcting quantum memories.
motivation: To find quantum memories that can protect information with minimal active error correction, leveraging self-correcting properties.
method: The authors introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees against local stochastic noise, and analyze the energy barrier and code parameters.
result: Layer codes achieve optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, and the decoding algorithms provide efficient error correction with provable performance.
conclusion: Layer codes are promising candidates for partially self-correcting quantum memories, potentially reducing the overhead of active error correction in quantum computing and communication.

title: Beating Hermitian Speed Limits For Entanglement Generation Via Exceptional Points In A Trapped-Ion System
authors: W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, And M. Feng
abstract:
Author(s): W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, and M. Feng

Entanglement generation is a cornerstone of quantum information science, yet its speed in Hermitian systems is fundamentally constrained by the coupling strength, a restriction known as the quantum speed limit. Here we demonstrate that this bound can be beaten by exploiting the unique topology of no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210201] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Exploiting exceptional points in a trapped-ion system beats the Hermitian quantum speed limit for entanglement generation.
motivation: To overcome the fundamental speed limit for entanglement generation imposed by coupling strength in Hermitian systems.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system engineered to have exceptional points (non-Hermitian degeneracies) to accelerate entanglement generation.
result: They demonstrate that entanglement can be generated faster than the Hermitian quantum speed limit by exploiting the topology of exceptional points.
conclusion: This work opens new avenues for fast entanglement generation in quantum information processing and challenges conventional speed limits.

title: Quantum Transition Rates In Arbitrary Physical Processes
authors: Adolfo Del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, And Seong-Ho Shinn
abstract:
Author(s): Adolfo del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, and Seong-Ho Shinn

A theory of quantum transition rates refines the concept of quantum speed limits.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210202] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of quantum transition rates that refines quantum speed limits, providing a framework to bound the speed of quantum processes.
motivation: Quantum speed limits set fundamental bounds on evolution times, but a general theory of transition rates for arbitrary processes was lacking. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors derive a general expression for quantum transition rates using the concept of quantum speed limits and the geometry of quantum state space, likely employing techniques from quantum information geometry and optimal control.
result: They obtain a unified framework that yields tighter bounds on transition rates than previous speed limits, applicable to both unitary and open system dynamics.
conclusion: The results have implications for understanding the energy-time trade-off in quantum processes, potentially impacting the design of faster quantum algorithms and the thermodynamics of quantum operations.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect Induced By Non-Markovian Exceptional Points
authors: Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, And Wei Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, and Wei Wu

Quantum Mpemba effect describes an anomalous phenomenon of accelerated relaxation, which is of fundamental interest in the field of nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Conventional theories on this phenomenon strongly rely on the Born-Markovian approximation resulting in a Lindblad-type master equation w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210402] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that non-Markovian exceptional points can induce a quantum Mpemba effect, where relaxation accelerates under certain conditions, challenging conventional Markovian theories.
motivation: To understand the role of non-Markovianity in anomalous relaxation phenomena like the Mpemba effect, which has implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze a quantum system coupled to a non-Markovian environment, identifying exceptional points in the Liouvillian spectrum that lead to accelerated relaxation.
result: They demonstrate that non-Markovian exceptional points can cause a quantum Mpemba effect, where the system relaxes faster when initially farther from equilibrium, contrary to typical behavior.
conclusion: This work extends the understanding of the Mpemba effect to non-Markovian regimes, suggesting new ways to control relaxation in quantum systems and potential applications in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Sensing Enabled By Scrambling-Induced Genuine Multipartite Entanglement
authors: Guantian Hu, Wenxuan Zhang, Zhihua Chen, Liuzhu Zhong, Jingchao Zhao, Chilong Liu, Zixing Liu, Yue Xu, Yongchang Lin, Yougui Ri, Guixu Xie, Mingze Liu, Haolan Yuan, Yuxuan Zhou, Yu Zhang, Chang-Kang Hu, Song Liu, Dian Tan, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Guantian Hu, Wenxuan Zhang, Zhihua Chen, Liuzhu Zhong, Jingchao Zhao, Chilong Liu, Zixing Liu, Yue Xu, Yongchang Lin, Yougui Ri, Guixu Xie, Mingze Liu, Haolan Yuan, Yuxuan Zhou, Yu Zhang, Chang-Kang Hu, Song Liu, Dian Tan, and Dapeng Yu

Quantum sensing leverages quantum resources to surpass the standard quantum limit, yet many existing protocols rely on the preparation of complex entangled states and Hamiltonian engineering, posing challenges for universality and scalability. Here, we report an experimental implementation of a univ…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210801] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates experimentally that scrambling dynamics in a quantum system can generate genuine multipartite entanglement, which is then used to enhance sensing precision beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of preparing complex entangled states for quantum sensing by using natural scrambling dynamics as a resource.
method: The authors implement a universal protocol on a superconducting quantum processor where a unitary scrambling circuit generates genuine multipartite entanglement, and then use the entangled state for parameter estimation.
result: They observe that the generated multipartite entanglement leads to a sensing precision that surpasses the standard quantum limit, demonstrating a practical advantage.
conclusion: Scrambling-induced entanglement offers a scalable and universal approach to quantum-enhanced sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and many-body physics.

title: Latent Splitting As A Causal Probe
authors: Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, And Rafael Chaves
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, and Rafael Chaves

Generalizations of Bell's framework to causal networks have yielded foundational insights and applications, including the use of interventions to enhance the detection of nonclassicality in scenarios with communication. Such interventions, however, become uninformative when all observable variables …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062415] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a causal inference method called latent splitting to probe nonclassicality in causal networks, extending Bell's framework to scenarios with communication.
motivation: To overcome limitations of standard interventions in detecting nonclassicality when all observable variables are involved, and to provide a more informative causal probe.
method: The authors propose latent splitting, a technique that splits latent nodes in a causal network to create new observable correlations, and analyze its effectiveness using Bell inequalities and entropy-based criteria.
result: Latent splitting can reveal nonclassical correlations that are hidden under standard interventions, and it provides a new tool for device-independent quantum information tasks.
conclusion: The work opens avenues for enhanced detection of quantum nonlocality in complex causal structures and may have implications for quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, and Da Zhang

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system, providing a new source for multiphoton entanglement.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are crucial for quantum information protocols, but generating them efficiently is challenging. Previous methods in hot atomic ensembles required complex fifth-order nonlinear processes.
method: The authors use a six-level cold atomic system with electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to produce energy-time-entangled triphotons via a cascaded spontaneous four-wave mixing process.
result: They successfully generated energy-time-entangled triphotons with high purity and coherence, verified by correlation measurements and violation of a Bell-type inequality.
conclusion: This work provides a practical source of multiphoton entanglement for quantum communication and networks, with potential for integration into quantum repeaters and entanglement distillation schemes.

title: Exact Many-body Quantum Dynamics In One-dimensional Baths Via Collective Spins
authors: Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, And Ana Asenjo-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, and Ana Asenjo-Garcia

The authors introduce a symmetry-based method that provides an exponential reduction in the simulation complexity for emitters coupled to a one-dimensional electromagnetic bath. Partial permutational symmetry is exploited to group qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom, allowing for a study of the superradiant burst scaling, the spin length of the collective system, and the metrological properties of the dark states.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061701] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A symmetry-based method reduces simulation complexity for emitters coupled to 1D baths, enabling exact study of superradiance and metrological properties.
motivation: Simulating many-body quantum dynamics in 1D baths is computationally expensive; the authors aim to exploit partial permutational symmetry to achieve exponential reduction.
method: They group qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom using partial permutational symmetry, mapping the problem to a collective spin model.
result: The method allows exact simulation of superradiant burst scaling, spin length dynamics, and metrological properties of dark states.
conclusion: This approach enables efficient study of collective phenomena in 1D baths, with implications for quantum metrology and understanding superradiance.

title: Probability-phase Mutual Information
authors: Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, And Fabio Anza
abstract:
Author(s): Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, and Fabio Anza

Quantum coherence is an exquisitely quantum phenomenon that depends on both probability amplitudes and relative phases. Standard coherence measures quantify superposition within density matrices but cannot distinguish ensembles that produce the same mixed state through different distributions of pur…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062413] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a new measure, probability-phase mutual information, that quantifies quantum coherence by distinguishing ensembles that yield the same mixed state but differ in phase distributions.
motivation: Standard coherence measures cannot differentiate between ensembles that produce the same mixed state via different distributions of pure states, limiting their ability to capture phase information.
method: The authors define probability-phase mutual information based on the mutual information between the probability distribution of measurement outcomes and the relative phase distribution of pure states in an ensemble.
result: The new measure successfully distinguishes ensembles that are indistinguishable by standard coherence measures, providing a finer-grained characterization of quantum coherence.
conclusion: This work offers a novel tool for studying quantum coherence and may have implications for quantum information theory and thermodynamics, particularly in contexts where phase information is crucial.

title: Quantum Viscosity Mechanism Of Dissipative Dynamics In The Dicke Model Expressed Via Lindblad Equation Of Motion
authors: M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, And S. I. Mukhin
abstract:
Author(s): M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, and S. I. Mukhin

Quantum dissipation is studied in the superradiant phase of the extended Dicke model. It is demonstrated analytically by quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant state coupled to Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath that the effective viscosity appearin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063706] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant phase coupled to a Caldeira-Leggett bath, revealing an effective viscosity mechanism for quantum dissipation.
motivation: To understand quantum dissipation in the superradiant phase of the Dicke model, which is relevant for hybrid quantum systems and superradiance.
method: Quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad equation for the extended Dicke model coupled to a Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath.
result: Demonstrated analytically that effective viscosity appears in the dissipative dynamics of the superradiant phase.
conclusion: Provides a microscopic foundation for dissipation in superradiant systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum devices.

title: Fluxonium Qubit-based Hybrid Electromechanical System
authors: Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, And Vibhor Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, and Vibhor Singh

Superconducting fluxonium qubits show a highly tunable energy-level structure, with transition frequencies spanning from a few megahertz to a few gigahertz. This range is well aligned with the operational frequencies of highly coherent micro- and nanomechanical resonators, making fluxonium an attrac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063707] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid system coupling a fluxonium qubit to a mechanical resonator, leveraging the qubit's wide frequency tunability for quantum transduction and sensing.
motivation: To exploit the fluxonium qubit's broad frequency range (MHz to GHz) to interface with high-coherence mechanical resonators, enabling new hybrid quantum devices.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a fluxonium qubit capacitively coupled to a mechanical resonator, deriving the Hamiltonian and studying the coupling strength, coherence, and tunability.
result: They show that the fluxonium qubit can be tuned to match mechanical resonance frequencies, achieving strong coupling and enabling coherent state transfer and entanglement.
conclusion: The fluxonium-mechanical system is a promising platform for quantum transducers and hybrid quantum networks, with potential for sensing and information processing.

title: Failure Of Epistemic Models To Explain The Antidistinguishability Of Quantum Mixed Preparations
authors: Sagnik Ray, Visweshwaran R, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Sagnik Ray, Visweshwaran R, and Debashis Saha

We investigate the limits of epistemic models in reproducing the empirical predictions of general quantum preparations. This involves comparing the common quantum overlap determined by the antidistinguishability of a set of preparations with the common epistemic overlap of the probability distributi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062203] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that epistemic models cannot reproduce the antidistinguishability of quantum mixed preparations, revealing a fundamental limitation of such models.
motivation: To understand whether epistemic interpretations of quantum theory can account for the phenomenon of antidistinguishability, which is a key feature of quantum preparations.
method: The authors compare the common quantum overlap (derived from antidistinguishability) with the common epistemic overlap of probability distributions in ontological models, using a framework of general quantum preparations.
result: They find that for certain sets of mixed preparations, the common epistemic overlap must exceed the common quantum overlap, implying that no epistemic model can reproduce the quantum predictions.
conclusion: This result strengthens the case against ψ-epistemic interpretations and highlights the need for non-epistemic (ontic) elements in quantum foundations.

title: Honest-binding Quantum Bit Commitment From Separable Operations
authors: Ziad Chaoui, Anna Pappa, And Matteo Rosati
abstract:
Author(s): Ziad Chaoui, Anna Pappa, and Matteo Rosati

Bit commitment is a fundamental cryptographic primitive and a cornerstone for numerous two-party cryptographic protocols, including zero-knowledge proofs. However, it has been proven that unconditionally secure bit commitment, both classical and quantum, is impossible. In this work, we demonstrate t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that quantum bit commitment with honest binding can be achieved using only separable operations, challenging previous impossibility results.
motivation: Bit commitment is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but unconditionally secure bit commitment is impossible. This work explores whether weaker security notions, such as honest binding, can be achieved under restricted operations.
method: The authors analyze the security of quantum bit commitment protocols where the parties are restricted to separable operations, using information-theoretic arguments and semidefinite programming.
result: They demonstrate that honest-binding quantum bit commitment is possible under separable operations, providing explicit protocols and security proofs.
conclusion: This result opens new avenues for practical quantum cryptography with limited quantum resources, and suggests that separability constraints can enable otherwise impossible tasks.

title: Probing Time-reversal-symmetry Breaking Using A Nonlinear Superconducting Ring Resonator
authors: Nicolas Dirnegger, Marie Wesson, Arpit Arora, Ioannis Petrides, Jonathan B. Curtis, Emily M. Been, Amir Yacoby, And Prineha Narang
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Dirnegger, Marie Wesson, Arpit Arora, Ioannis Petrides, Jonathan B. Curtis, Emily M. Been, Amir Yacoby, and Prineha Narang

The authors suggest a way to detect time-reversal-symmetry breaking using a driven-dissipative superconducting ring resonator. In particular, nonlinear interactions can enforce symmetric steady-state photon populations, which become asymmetric when even weak symmetry breaking is present, allowing for a sensitive probe of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking effects in quantum materials and providing an interesting use case for superconducting microwave resonators outside of quantum information processing.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A nonlinear superconducting ring resonator is proposed as a sensitive probe of time-reversal-symmetry breaking via asymmetric steady-state photon populations.
motivation: To detect weak time-reversal-symmetry breaking in quantum materials, which is challenging with existing techniques.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a driven-dissipative superconducting ring resonator with Kerr nonlinearity, showing that symmetric steady-state photon populations become asymmetric under time-reversal-symmetry breaking.
result: Nonlinear interactions enforce symmetric populations in the symmetric case, but even weak symmetry breaking leads to detectable asymmetry, enabling sensitive probing.
conclusion: This provides a new use case for superconducting microwave resonators beyond quantum information processing, with potential applications in detecting symmetry-breaking effects in quantum materials.

title: Thermodynamic Framework For Spin-orbit-torque–driven Skyrmions: Bridging Spin Dynamics And Energy Dissipation
authors: Haohua Wen And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Haohua Wen and Yue Zheng

Magnetic skyrmions driven by spin-orbit torque (SOT) are promising for energy-efficient spintronics. However, their description relies on dynamical models treating dissipation phenomenologically, leaving the fundamental dynamics-dissipation link unresolved. Here, we establish a thermodynamic framewo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214417] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a thermodynamic framework for spin-orbit-torque-driven skyrmions, linking spin dynamics to energy dissipation.
motivation: Existing models treat dissipation phenomenologically, leaving the fundamental dynamics-dissipation link unresolved. The authors aim to bridge this gap for skyrmions, which are promising for energy-efficient spintronics.
method: The authors establish a thermodynamic framework that connects spin dynamics with energy dissipation, likely using nonequilibrium thermodynamics and micromagnetic simulations.
result: The framework provides a quantitative description of energy dissipation during skyrmion motion driven by spin-orbit torque, revealing the thermodynamic cost of skyrmion dynamics.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding of energy dissipation in spintronic devices and may guide the design of more energy-efficient skyrmion-based technologies.

title: Boltzmann Sampling By Diabatic Quantum Annealing
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Yongjoo Baek
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Yongjoo Baek

Boltzmann sampling is a central component of many computational frameworks, including numerous algorithms in machine learning. Although quantum annealers have been investigated as potential fast Boltzmann samplers, their dependence on environmental noise makes precise control of the effective temper…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065302] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a diabatic quantum annealing protocol for Boltzmann sampling that enables precise control of effective temperature without relying on environmental noise.
motivation: Boltzmann sampling is crucial for machine learning, but quantum annealers typically depend on environmental noise for temperature control, which limits precision. The authors aim to achieve controllable Boltzmann sampling using a diabatic approach.
method: The authors introduce a diabatic quantum annealing protocol where the system is driven out of equilibrium in a controlled manner, and the effective temperature is tuned via the annealing schedule. They analyze the protocol using a two-level system model and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that the diabatic protocol can produce Boltzmann distributions with a tunable effective temperature, independent of the bath temperature, and show that the sampling fidelity can be high for appropriate schedules.
conclusion: The work provides a new method for Boltzmann sampling on quantum annealers with precise temperature control, potentially benefiting machine learning and other computational tasks. Future work may extend to larger systems and more complex distributions.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on the simultaneous presence of local quantum coherence and global correlations (mutual information) in quantum systems.
method: The authors experimentally realize a quantum system and measure both local coherence and quantum mutual information, observing that their sum is bounded by a fixed upper limit.
result: The sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded, indicating a trade-off: increasing one resource necessarily decreases the other.
conclusion: This trade-off provides insight into the resource theory of quantum coherence and correlations, with implications for quantum information processing and the design of quantum protocols.

title: Near-ultimate Quantum-enhanced Sensitivity In Dissipative Critical Sensing With Partial Access
authors: Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, and Victor Montenegro

Quantum sensors are powerful devices that exploit quantum effects to detect minute quantities with extremely high precision. Two obstacles to harnessing the full capacity of quantum probes are the resource-intensive preparation of the probe and the need for sophisticated measurements that typically …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023241] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that dissipative critical sensing with partial access can achieve near-ultimate quantum-enhanced sensitivity, overcoming resource and measurement limitations.
motivation: Quantum sensors face obstacles from resource-intensive probe preparation and sophisticated measurements; this work aims to achieve high sensitivity with minimal resources and partial access.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a dissipative critical sensor near a phase transition, using a Lindblad master equation to model the open system dynamics and deriving the quantum Fisher information for partial measurement access.
result: They show that even with partial access to the probe, the sensitivity scales near the Heisenberg limit, and the critical point enhances the signal-to-noise ratio despite dissipation.
conclusion: The results suggest that practical, resource-efficient quantum sensors can be realized using dissipative critical systems, with implications for quantum metrology and information thermodynamics.

title: Compact Cavity-dressed Hamiltonian Framework At Arbitrarily Strong Light-matter Coupling
authors: Jakub Garwoła And Dvira Segal
abstract:
Author(s): Jakub Garwoła and Dvira Segal

Researchers derive a nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized field modes and apply it to the open Rabi model and the Dicke-Heisenberg lattice model. They demonstrate advantage over conventional approaches in terms of error scaling with Hilbert space dimension and reveal cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically, achieving computational savings over brute-force simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022039] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized fields is developed and applied to the open Rabi and Dicke-Heisenberg lattice models, showing improved error scaling and computational savings.
motivation: Standard perturbative methods fail at strong light-matter coupling, and brute-force simulations become intractable for large Hilbert spaces. The authors aim to provide an efficient nonperturbative framework.
method: They derive a compact cavity-dressed Hamiltonian framework that maps the strongly coupled system to a weakly coupled one via a polaron-like transformation, enabling perturbative treatment of the residual coupling.
result: The method yields better error scaling with Hilbert space dimension compared to conventional approaches, and reveals cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically with significant computational savings.
conclusion: This framework enables efficient simulation of strongly coupled light-matter systems, with potential applications to quantum transducers and hybrid quantum systems, and can be extended to more complex models.

title: Measuring Temporal Entropies In Experiments
authors: Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, And Luca Tagliacozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, and Luca Tagliacozzo

We propose an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems. Our approach involves using local operators as probes to characterize the out-of-equilibrium dynamics induced by a geometric double quench on a replicated system. Such protocol mimics the path…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023229] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems using local operators and a geometric double quench on a replicated system.
motivation: To develop a practical method for characterizing out-of-equilibrium dynamics and entropy production in quantum systems, which is central to information thermodynamics.
method: Uses local operators as probes and a geometric double quench on a replicated system to mimic the path integral for temporal entropies, enabling experimental measurement.
result: The protocol allows extraction of generalized temporal entropies from experimental data, providing insights into the entropy dynamics of many-body quantum systems.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and experiment for temporal entropies, with implications for understanding irreversibility and energy consumption in quantum processes.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) for space-based systems, separating Doppler and gravitational contributions.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication involves high relative velocities and gravitational potentials, which cause frequency shifts that can degrade CV-QKD performance. Understanding these shifts is crucial for practical implementation.
method: The authors start from general relativistic considerations and systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, transverse Doppler, and gravitational redshift components. They model the effect on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how relativistic effects impact the secure key rate and provide bounds for tolerable velocity and altitude variations.
conclusion: The work provides essential corrections for designing space-based CV-QKD systems and highlights the need to account for relativistic effects in future quantum communication networks.

title: Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks: Learning Dissipative Dynamics Via Contact Variational Principles
authors: Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, And Gang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, and Gang Yan

Physics-informed machine learning has proven effective for learning conservative dynamical systems. However, most real-world systems are nonconservative, and current approaches typically handle dissipation through ad hoc modifications or require access to full-state information. Here, we introduce t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023224] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks, a physics-informed machine learning framework for learning dissipative dynamics from data using contact geometry.
motivation: Most real-world systems are nonconservative, and existing physics-informed ML methods either require full-state information or handle dissipation via ad hoc modifications, limiting their applicability.
method: The authors propose a neural network architecture based on the Herglotz variational principle, which naturally incorporates dissipation through contact geometry, enabling learning of dissipative dynamics from partial observations.
result: The method accurately learns dissipative dynamics (e.g., damped harmonic oscillator, Van der Pol oscillator) from limited data, outperforming standard approaches in data efficiency and generalization.
conclusion: This work bridges contact geometry and machine learning, offering a principled way to model nonconservative systems, with potential applications in thermodynamics and control.

title: Controlled Buildup Of Half-quantized Thermal Conductance In An Engineered Chiral Spin Liquid Platform
authors: Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Nathan Goldman

We study thermal transport along the edge of a small chiral spin liquid device coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs, a platform suitable for quantum-engineered systems. Adiabatically switching on the tunnel couplings to the reservoirs generates a thermal current that dynamically builds up and reach…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023226] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled buildup of half-quantized thermal conductance in a chiral spin liquid platform coupled to Ising-chain reservoirs, relevant to engineered quantum systems.
motivation: To study thermal transport in chiral spin liquids, which are exotic phases with potential applications in quantum information, and to understand how edge modes contribute to quantized thermal conductance in small engineered devices.
method: The authors model a small chiral spin liquid device coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs, adiabatically switching on tunnel couplings to generate a thermal current. They analyze the dynamic buildup of thermal conductance using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the thermal conductance builds up to a half-quantized value, reflecting the fractionalized edge excitations of the chiral spin liquid, and that this buildup is controlled by the coupling strength and system size.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for observing quantized thermal transport in engineered quantum systems, with implications for probing topological order and designing quantum devices.

title: Impossibility Of Quantum Private Queries
authors: Esther Hänggi And Severin Winkler
abstract:
Author(s): Esther Hänggi and Severin Winkler

This work investigates whether quantum communication protocols allow confidential access to a remote database. It shows that any protocol that does not reveal which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022036] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that any quantum private query protocol that hides which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database, showing a fundamental limitation.
motivation: To determine whether quantum communication can provide secure private database queries without revealing the queried item, addressing a key question in quantum cryptography.
method: The authors use information-theoretic arguments and quantum communication complexity to analyze the impossibility of quantum private queries, likely employing entropy or distinguishability measures.
result: They show that any protocol with perfect privacy for the user (i.e., the database does not learn which item is retrieved) necessarily allows the user to learn all database entries, thus no such protocol can be secure.
conclusion: The result establishes a fundamental trade-off between user privacy and database security in quantum private queries, implying that alternative approaches or relaxed security definitions are needed.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Photon loss is a major obstacle in quantum communication and computing; active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive. This work explores a passive approach to reach the breakeven point where error correction begins to extend qubit lifetime.
method: The researchers implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives (no active measurements) in a superconducting circuit or similar platform, likely employing a bosonic code such as the cat code or binomial code to protect against photon loss.
result: They demonstrate that the qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit, achieving the breakeven point where the error-corrected qubit outperforms the uncorrected one.
conclusion: This work shows that passive error correction can be effective against photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum error correction in communication and memory applications. Future work may extend to other error types and integrate with quantum repeaters.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: To overcome the rate-distance limitations of discrete-variable QKD and improve the practicality of continuous-variable QKD by achieving high secret key rates with composable security.
method: The authors combine discrete modulation (e.g., QPSK) with continuous-variable QKD and employ advanced security analysis tools (e.g., entropy accumulation theorem) to prove composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 100 km, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: This work brings high-speed, secure quantum communication closer to practical deployment, and the security proof framework can be extended to other discrete-modulated CV-QKD protocols.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for understanding qubit leakage and improving readout in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Transmon qubits can ionize into highly excited states, causing computational errors. Understanding the dynamics of these transitions is essential for developing better readout schemes and mitigating leakage.
method: The authors experimentally probe transmon ionization using microwave spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements, analyzing multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They identify specific multiphoton resonance conditions that lead to ionization and characterize the transition rates, showing that ionization occurs via Landau-Zener tunneling at avoided crossings.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, guiding the design of improved readout and control protocols to enhance transmon qubit fidelity.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: Midcircuit measurement recording can exponentially extend quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Quantum information is fragile and decays quickly; finding strategies to preserve it is crucial for quantum computing and algorithms.
method: The authors study monitored quantum dynamics where midcircuit measurements are recorded, analyzing the scaling of quantum information lifetime with system size and measurement rate.
result: Recording measurement outcomes leads to an exponentially long quantum information lifetime, contrasting with the usual exponential decay without recording.
conclusion: This work provides a practical strategy to protect quantum information in near-term devices and opens avenues for understanding information thermodynamics in monitored systems.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for scalable quantum error correction, especially in the presence of environmental radiation.
method: Experimental study of a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, measuring phase error correlations and burst dynamics.
result: Radiation induces spatially and temporally correlated phase error bursts that can overwhelm error correction codes even with state-of-the-art shielding.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies or hardware designs are needed to protect against radiation-induced correlated errors in quantum processors.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process due to electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: To understand heating dynamics and thermalization in mesoscopic electron baths under high magnetic fields, which is relevant for quantum information processing and low-temperature thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved noise thermometry was used to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: A two-step thermalization process was observed, attributed to the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into energy dissipation and thermalization in mesoscopic systems, with implications for quantum device operation and information thermodynamics.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with integrated passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance, protecting qubits from thermal backaction and enabling scalable isolator-free readout.
motivation: Superconducting qubits require low-noise amplification for readout, but conventional isolators and circulators introduce loss and are bulky. This work aims to eliminate the need for isolators by integrating reverse isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier (TWPA) using Josephson junctions, incorporating passive reverse isolation through directional coupling or nonreciprocal elements to suppress backaction from the output chain.
result: The amplifier achieves near-quantum-limited noise performance while providing >20 dB of reverse isolation, protecting qubits from thermal noise emitted by subsequent amplification stages.
conclusion: This isolator-free readout architecture simplifies superconducting quantum computer wiring, reduces loss, and improves scalability, with potential impact on quantum error correction and multiplexed readout.

title: Harnessing Quantum Backaction For Time-Series Processing
authors: Giacomo Franceschetto, Marcin Płodzień, Maciej Lewenstein, Antonio Acín, And Pere Mujal
abstract:
Author(s): Giacomo Franceschetto, Marcin Płodzień, Maciej Lewenstein, Antonio Acín, and Pere Mujal

Tuning the strength of indirect measurements in quantum reservoir computing is shown to enhance memory and performance for processing time-series data, providing a way to turn quantum backaction into a resource.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021002] Published Thu Apr 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that tuning the strength of indirect measurements in quantum reservoir computing can enhance memory and performance for time-series processing, turning quantum backaction into a resource.
motivation: To explore how quantum backaction, typically considered detrimental, can be harnessed as a resource for information processing tasks, specifically in the context of quantum reservoir computing for time-series analysis.
method: The authors use a quantum reservoir computing framework where indirect measurements are performed on a quantum system, and the measurement strength is tuned to optimize the reservoir's memory and computational performance.
result: They find that by adjusting the measurement strength, the quantum reservoir can achieve enhanced memory capacity and improved performance on time-series prediction tasks, effectively utilizing quantum backaction.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on quantum backaction as a controllable resource, with implications for quantum machine learning and hybrid quantum systems where measurement-induced dynamics can be exploited.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate frequency ranges. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts to measure noise cross-correlations, enabling extraction of noise spectra in previously inaccessible frequency bands.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, demonstrating its ability to characterize noise in the intermediate-frequency regime, which is relevant for qubit decoherence.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise spectroscopy in quantum devices, with implications for improving qubit performance and understanding noise sources in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade with system size, enabling strong antibunching and high transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: To overcome the need for strong single-emitter coupling in conventional photon blockade, which is experimentally challenging, by leveraging collective effects in ensembles.
method: Theoretical analysis of an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, studying the dependence of photon blockade on system size and coupling strengths.
result: Photon blockade is collectively enhanced, with antibunching improving and transmission remaining high as the number of emitters increases, even for weak single-emitter coupling.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics at the few-photon level.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: To overcome performance limitations of existing Josephson mixers, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: Design and experimental characterization of impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, focusing on bandwidth and saturation power improvements.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to traditional designs, allowing for efficient amplification and transduction of quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for scalable quantum computing and communication systems, particularly in hybrid quantum systems where efficient signal conversion is critical.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of energy relaxation errors in superconducting qubits by converting them into erasure errors that are easier to detect and correct.
