method: The authors leverage the parity symmetry of integer fluxonium qubits and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasures.
result: The conversion of relaxation errors into erasures significantly boosts the effective coherence times of the qubits.
conclusion: This erasure conversion technique offers a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting circuits, and future work may extend it to other qubit modalities.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a system that mimics a mechanical oscillator with negative effective mass.
result: They demonstrate coherent cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a cavity-mode multiplexing scheme to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, addressing scalability challenges.
motivation: Cavity-enhanced operations are powerful for quantum information processing but are typically limited to a single atom or small ensembles; scaling to large arrays is a key challenge.
method: The authors introduce a method to multiplex multiple cavity modes (e.g., using spatial or frequency multiplexing) so that each atom in a 2D array interacts with a distinct cavity mode, enabling parallel operations.
result: They demonstrate theoretically and with proof-of-principle experiments that mode multiplexing can achieve high-fidelity parallel operations across many atoms without crosstalk, significantly increasing the scale of cavity-enhanced neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum computing and simulation with neutral atoms, and could be combined with other hybrid quantum systems for enhanced functionality.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a superconducting quantum device, achieving >99.9% fidelity for all operations.
motivation: To advance scalable quantum computing by improving gate and readout fidelities in superconducting circuits, which are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol were used to optimize gate and readout performance in a single superconducting device.
result: Simultaneous single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout all achieved fidelities above 99.9%.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that high-fidelity operations are achievable in a single device, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive. The authors aim to reduce the cost by using partially randomized time evolution.
method: They introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzing the trade-off between randomization and error in the context of phase estimation.
result: The method achieves orders-of-magnitude reduction in the number of Trotter steps needed for a given accuracy, as demonstrated on quantum chemistry benchmarks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical technique to lower the overhead of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices, and opens avenues for further optimization of randomized Hamiltonian simulation.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Haar-random quantum codes exhibit a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise, with a simple mechanism governing the transition.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits and phase structure of quantum error-correcting codes under realistic local noise, which is crucial for practical quantum communication and computation.
method: Analytical and numerical study of spectral properties of Haar-random quantum codes, analyzing the transition in decoding capability as a function of noise strength and code parameters.
result: Identified a simple mechanism for the decodable-to-nondecodable transition, characterized by spectral properties of the code's density matrix under local noise.
conclusion: Provides insight into the design of quantum codes and the nature of error correction transitions, with implications for quantum communication and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for quantum information processing in hybrid systems combining continuous-variable (oscillator) and discrete-variable (qudit) degrees of freedom, which are relevant for platforms like superconducting circuits coupled to spin ensembles.
method: The authors generalize the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems using symplectic operations over a ring, and construct stabilizer states and codes based on noncommutative geometry.
result: They define hybrid stabilizer states and codes, demonstrate scalable error correction, and show potential improvements in displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for hybrid quantum processors, enabling new error-correcting codes and sensing applications, with implications for quantum repeaters and networks.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrates that non-Gaussian operations can surpass these limits, enabling access to colder states.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to near ground states is crucial for quantum technologies, but the role of Gaussian vs. non-Gaussian resources in achieving low temperatures was not fully understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Gaussian constraints and analyze cooling protocols using both Gaussian and non-Gaussian operations, deriving bounds and demonstrating enhancements.
result: Gaussian operations impose a fundamental limit on the achievable temperature, while non-Gaussian resources (e.g., photon subtraction) can overcome this limit and yield significantly colder states.
conclusion: The work provides a clear operational distinction between Gaussian and non-Gaussian cooling, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the design of efficient cooling protocols.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on information storage and transmission in quantum memories under Markovian noise using information-theoretic tools.
motivation: To understand the ultimate capabilities of noisy quantum memories for storing and transmitting quantum information, which is crucial for quantum computing and communication.
method: The authors employ information-theoretic analysis, likely using entropy and mutual information measures, to characterize the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory channels.
result: Key findings include bounds on the storage and transmission rates of quantum information in the presence of Markovian noise, possibly identifying optimal error correction strategies.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical benchmarks for quantum memory performance and may guide the design of error-correcting codes and noise mitigation techniques.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a Kerr parametric oscillator to simulate dissipative quantum dynamics relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating a hybrid quantum simulation approach.
motivation: To explore quantum simulation of chemical reactions using a superconducting circuit platform, specifically focusing on dissipative processes that are challenging for classical computers.
method: A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator is employed as a quantum simulator, with asymmetry control to map the system's dynamics to a chemical activation model.
result: The parametric oscillator successfully reproduces key features of chemical activation, including barrier crossing and dissipation effects, showing good agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical quantum simulation of chemical dynamics using a superconducting circuit, opening avenues for studying complex chemical reactions with quantum hardware.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro
abstract:
Author(s): Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, and Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor, enabling concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and precision of multiparameter estimation in quantum sensing by leveraging entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin.
method: Experimental implementation using a solid-state quantum sensor (likely NV center) with an electronic spin and a nuclear spin ancilla, employing entanglement to perform simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters.
result: Entanglement allows concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence, enhancing estimation precision beyond classical limits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates practical benefits of entanglement in quantum sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and quantum information processing, and suggests future extensions to more complex sensors.

title: Hardware-Efficient Universal Linear Transformations For Optical Modes In The Synthetic Time Dimension
authors: Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, and Saikat Guha

A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity while maintaining all-to-all connectivity, exceeding performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020305] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity for universal linear transformations, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: To overcome hardware scalability challenges in optical quantum computing by reducing the number of physical components needed for universal linear transformations.
method: The authors propose a photonic processor that uses a synthetic time dimension to achieve all-to-all connectivity with exponentially fewer hardware resources, and analyze its performance under realistic physical constraints.
result: The processor exceeds performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation, demonstrating a hardware-efficient approach to linear optical transformations.
conclusion: This work paves the way for more practical and scalable optical quantum computers, with potential applications in quantum communication and information processing.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond quantum key distribution, addressing the growing need for diverse quantum-enhanced security tasks.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for various quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum money, bit commitment, oblivious transfer) and discusses experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It categorizes quantum cryptographic protocols, explains their security definitions and limitations, and surveys current photonic experimental achievements.
conclusion: The review highlights the potential and challenges of quantum cryptography beyond QKD, suggesting future work on practical implementations and security proofs.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: This review classifies universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum systems using quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal behavior lacks a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify stationary states based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking them to underlying symmetries and topological features.
conclusion: The classification provides a foundation for understanding and engineering nonequilibrium phases, with implications for quantum technologies and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is non-classical and non-quantum, focusing on tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement.
motivation: To address the possibility that gravity is neither classical nor quantum, and to propose concrete experiments that can constrain new theories of gravity.
method: Information-theoretic analysis of thought experiments and review of proposed tabletop-scale experiments for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE).
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing how entanglement generation can test the quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods provide a concrete way to probe the nature of gravity, with tabletop experiments offering near-term testability.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that minimizes the evolution time by maintaining a constant speed along the adiabatic path, achieving the rigorous lower bound.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, leading to long evolution times. The authors aim to optimize the schedule to achieve the theoretical lower bound on evolution time.
method: The authors derive a schedule that keeps the geometric speed constant, which is the speed along the adiabatic path measured by the metric induced by the quantum geometric tensor. They analyze the scaling of the evolution time with the path length and energy gap.
result: The constant geometric speed schedule achieves the rigorous lower bound on evolution time, scaling as O(L^2/Δ^2) where L is the adiabatic path length and Δ is the minimum gap, improving over traditional linear schedules.
conclusion: This work provides an optimal scheduling strategy for adiabatic state preparation, with implications for reducing energy consumption and improving efficiency in quantum algorithms and simulations.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes that enable constant-depth generation of magic states with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but are costly to produce; efficient generation is needed for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of high-rate quantum LDPC codes, and demonstrates their use for generating CZ magic states in constant depth using finite block-length analysis.
result: Tricycle codes achieve high noise resilience and efficient magic-state generation with constant-depth circuits, outperforming previous methods.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical path toward reducing overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computing, with implications for quantum error correction and resource-efficient quantum computation.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
motivation: To improve the accuracy of noise modeling in transmon quantum processors by capturing complex spatiotemporally correlated errors that standard Markovian models miss.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that accounts for correlated errors across space and time, and validate it using a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to conventional noise models when used as a proxy simulator.
conclusion: The approach enables more reliable simulation of near-term quantum devices, with implications for error mitigation and algorithm design in transmon-based processors.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a scheme for performing many parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves high-performance parallel measurements without requiring additional code blocks, preserving important code properties.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hardware-friendly quantum Gibbs sampling protocol using local circuits that achieves rapid mixing and high accuracy without block encoding.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum simulation and optimization, but existing methods often require complex operations like block encoding, which are challenging for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors replace block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a specific design that ensures rapid mixing and maintains accuracy, likely based on a quantum Markov chain or dissipative engineering approach.
result: The protocol achieves efficient Gibbs sampling with local circuits, demonstrating fast convergence to the target thermal state and high fidelity, as validated by theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for quantum thermal state preparation on current hardware, with implications for quantum simulation, optimization, and thermodynamics of quantum information processing.

title: Single-Enantiomer Spin Polarizers In Superconducting Junctions
authors: Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, And Jörg Kröger
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, and Jörg Kröger

A new experiment shows that spin-polarized currents conducted by helical organic molecules are not just a measurement artifact, as some researchers suspected.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226201] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that spin-polarized currents in superconducting junctions using helical organic molecules are genuine and not artifacts, supporting the field of chiral-induced spin selectivity.
motivation: To resolve controversy about whether spin-polarized currents from helical organic molecules are real or measurement artifacts, and to explore their integration with superconducting junctions.
method: Experimental setup with superconducting junctions incorporating helical organic molecules as spin filters, measuring spin-polarized transport properties.
result: Confirmed that single-enantiomer helical molecules produce robust spin polarization in superconducting junctions, ruling out artifact explanations.
conclusion: Validates chiral-induced spin selectivity for spintronics applications, potentially enabling new hybrid quantum systems combining molecular chirality with superconductivity.

title: Spin-Dependent Fluorescence Mediated By Antisymmetric Exchange In Triplet Exciton Pairs
authors: Yan Sun, G. Ricci, M. Monteverde, V. Derkach, T. Chanelière, E. Aldridge, D. Casanova, D. Beljonne, J. E. Anthony, And A. D. Chepelianskii
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Sun, G. Ricci, M. Monteverde, V. Derkach, T. Chanelière, E. Aldridge, D. Casanova, D. Beljonne, J. E. Anthony, and A. D. Chepelianskii

Singlet fission and triplet-triplet annihilation (TTA) are spin-dependent phenomena critical to optoelectronics. The dynamics of spin populations during geminate triplet pair separation are crucial for controlling fission and TTA rates. We show that the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) induce…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 216903] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in triplet exciton pairs can mediate spin-dependent fluorescence, offering a new mechanism to control singlet fission and triplet-triplet annihilation.
motivation: Understanding spin dynamics in geminate triplet pairs is crucial for optimizing optoelectronic devices. The role of antisymmetric exchange (DMI) in these processes was previously unexplored.
method: The authors combine theoretical modeling and experimental measurements on organic semiconductors to demonstrate DMI-induced spin mixing and its effect on fluorescence.
result: DMI leads to spin-dependent fluorescence modulation, enabling control over singlet fission and TTA rates via magnetic fields or material design.
conclusion: This work opens new avenues for spin control in organic optoelectronics and may impact quantum information processing using triplet excitons.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria under detection loophole conditions, finding that the PPT criterion is more robust.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world detectors have inefficiencies (detection loophole) that can affect the reliability of different detection methods.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and compare the positive partial transposition (PPT) criterion and moment-based criteria for entanglement detection in the presence of detection inefficiencies, modeling the detection loophole.
result: The PPT criterion detects a greater volume of entangled states than moment-based criteria in ideal setups, but under detection loophole conditions, the advantage persists and the PPT criterion remains more robust.
conclusion: The findings guide experimentalists in choosing entanglement detection methods that are resilient to detector inefficiencies, and highlight the need for further study of loophole effects in entanglement verification.

title: Quantum Tidal Locking In Orbiting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, And Xiaoji Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, and Xiaoji Zhou

Angular momentum coupling manifests widely in diverse physical systems, underpinning the emergent properties and collective dynamics across different scales. The tidal locking, which originates from the synchronization of rotational and orbital motions, has far-reaching impacts in celestial mechanic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically demonstrates quantum tidal locking in orbiting Bose-Einstein condensates, where angular momentum coupling leads to synchronization of rotational and orbital motion at the quantum level.
motivation: To explore quantum analogs of classical tidal locking, which is a ubiquitous phenomenon in celestial mechanics, and to understand angular momentum coupling in ultracold atomic systems.
method: The authors model two Bose-Einstein condensates in orbit around each other, using mean-field theory and quantum fluctuation analysis to study the dynamics of angular momentum transfer and synchronization.
result: They find that quantum fluctuations can induce a locking of the rotational frequency to the orbital frequency, analogous to classical tidal locking but with distinct quantum features such as entanglement and squeezing.
conclusion: This work opens a new direction for studying quantum synchronization and angular momentum coupling in mesoscopic systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and simulation of celestial mechanics.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in digital-analog quantum computing, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians to implement universal quantum operations.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a promising alternative to gate-based quantum computing by using natural system interactions as entangling resources, potentially reducing overhead. However, explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in this paradigm were lacking.
method: The authors derive analytical formulas for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians using the digital-analog approach, combining the system's natural interaction Hamiltonian with single-qubit gates.
result: They provide explicit decompositions and error bounds for Hamiltonian simulation, demonstrating the feasibility and efficiency of the digital-analog paradigm for a range of Hamiltonians.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for digital-analog quantum simulation, with implications for near-term quantum devices where natural interactions are strong and gate fidelities are limited.

title: Localization And Scattering Of A Photon In Quasiperiodic Qubit Arrays
authors: Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, And Chaohong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, and Chaohong Lee

We study the localization and scattering of a single photon in a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings. As the quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetime appear around the resonant frequency and form a continuum band. In stark c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063704] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies single-photon localization and scattering in waveguide-coupled qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings, revealing a continuum of long-lived subradiant states.
motivation: To understand how quasiperiodic disorder affects photon transport and localization in waveguide QED systems, which is relevant for quantum information processing and light-matter interfaces.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with spacings following a Fibonacci sequence, using a real-space formalism to compute photon scattering and bound-state properties.
result: As quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetimes emerge around the resonant frequency, forming a continuum band. These states are distinct from Anderson-localized modes and arise from the quasiperiodic order.
conclusion: The findings provide a new mechanism for engineering long-lived photon states in waveguide QED, with potential applications in quantum memory and slow-light devices. Future work could explore nonlinear effects and multi-photon dynamics.

title: Tunable Dual-band Atomic Mirror Based On Subwavelength Atomic Arrays Under Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, And Yan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, and Yan Zhang

Subwavelength atomic arrays offer a powerful platform for engineering cooperative light-matter interactions and enabling quantum metasurfaces. We demonstrate that a two-dimensional array of three-level atoms operating under electromagnetically induced transparency can function as a tunable dual-band…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063705] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A subwavelength array of three-level atoms under EIT acts as a tunable dual-band mirror with high reflectivity and narrow linewidths.
motivation: To engineer tunable, narrow-band mirrors for quantum metasurfaces and cooperative light-matter interactions using atomic arrays.
method: Theoretical analysis of a 2D array of three-level Λ-type atoms with EIT, calculating collective reflection and transmission spectra via coupled-dipole model.
result: The array exhibits two high-reflectivity bands corresponding to EIT transparency windows, with tunability via control field parameters and atomic density.
conclusion: This dual-band mirror can be used for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics at the single-photon level, with potential for integration into quantum networks.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines the super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial-order spin interactions.
motivation: To develop a protocol that suppresses noise from spin interactions, which is crucial for quantum state protection and quantum gyroscope applications.
method: The authors introduce a protocol that uses the quantum super-Zeno effect (frequent projective measurements) and spin-anticoherent subspaces (states that are maximally sensitive to rotations) to counteract unwanted spin dynamics.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations; for spin-1/2, average fidelity scales as 1 - F̄ ∝ t^4, showing improved protection.
conclusion: The protocol offers a new way to protect quantum states from certain types of noise, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, demonstrating efficient quantum operations in a high-dimensional Hilbert space.
motivation: To exploit the enhanced information density and potential efficiency of qudits over qubits, using single-molecule magnets as a platform.
method: The authors employ optimal control theory to design time-optimal pulses for a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, considering its energy level structure and coupling to external fields.
result: They achieve high-fidelity quantum gates with minimal operation time, showing that molecular spin qudits can be controlled efficiently.
conclusion: This work advances the use of molecular spin qudits for quantum information processing, with implications for hybrid quantum systems and quantum control.

title: Spin Entanglement Of Two Atoms Through Coupling To Their Thermal Motion
authors: Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, And Stuart S. Szigeti
abstract:
Author(s): Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, and Stuart S. Szigeti

The spin dynamics of two alkali-metal atoms in an optical tweezer is driven by spin-changing collisions that couple the spin state of the atoms to their relative motion. This paper experimentally studies the resulting spin states when the relative motion is in a thermal state with [MATH] much la…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062201] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates spin entanglement between two atoms mediated by their thermal relative motion via spin-changing collisions in an optical tweezer.
motivation: To understand how thermal motion, typically a source of decoherence, can be harnessed to generate entanglement between atomic spins.
method: Two alkali-metal atoms are trapped in an optical tweezer, and spin-changing collisions couple their spin states to their relative motional state, which is thermal. The resulting spin entanglement is characterized via state tomography.
result: The experiment shows that significant spin entanglement can be generated even when the relative motion is in a thermal state, with the degree of entanglement depending on temperature and interaction parameters.
conclusion: Thermal motion can be a resource for entanglement generation, offering a new mechanism for creating entangled states in atomic systems without requiring ground-state cooling.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional derivatives, revealing violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium thermodynamics in systems with long-range interactions and fractional dynamics, particularly how phase coexistence deviates from local equilibrium assumptions.
method: Numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, which modify the density of states at low wave numbers.
result: The system exhibits violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics during first-order phase transitions, with non-classical scaling of interface properties.
conclusion: Fractional derivatives introduce nonlocal effects that break local equilibrium, suggesting new thermodynamic behavior in systems with long-range interactions.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper optically probes phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond, revealing linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: To understand the coherence characteristics of SnV centers, which are promising for quantum applications, and to investigate phonon-induced decoherence mechanisms.
method: Optical spectroscopy and coherent population trapping experiments on SnV centers in diamond, analyzing linewidth broadening and ground-state orbital level dynamics.
result: Observed linewidth broadening due to phonon interactions and demonstrated coherent population trapping between ground-state orbital levels.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into phononic properties of SnV centers, aiding in the development of diamond-based quantum devices.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: To understand entropy contributions from spin and motional degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems, and to test the feasibility of isolating topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a two-dimensional electron gas in a partially filled Landau level, likely via a thermodynamic technique such as heat capacity or magnetization.
result: Observation of successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom as temperature is lowered, with entropy steps corresponding to known fractional quantum Hall states; sensitivity achieved that can constrain topological entropy.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path to measuring topological entropy in non-Abelian states, which is relevant for quantum information and thermodynamics of quantum operations.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A deep-level defect in ZnO with long coherence and high spin selectivity enables high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a solid-state spin defect in a wide-band-gap oxide that can serve as a scalable quantum platform, addressing the need for long coherence and efficient readout.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of the defect's electronic structure, spin coherence, and optical properties.
result: Discovery of a deep defect in ZnO with 4-ms spin coherence time, small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO defects are a promising new platform for scalable quantum technologies, with potential for quantum sensing, communication, and computing.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving high fidelity and reduced measurement time.
motivation: Quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting their use in protocols like entanglement distillation and quantum error correction. The goal was to develop a readout that is more quantum nondemolition (QND) to preserve quantum states.
method: The authors implemented an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, applied to a multilevel qudit system (e.g., a spin-7/2 nucleus).
result: The protocol achieved a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors, demonstrating improved QND character.
conclusion: This adaptive readout enhances the performance of quantum measurements, which is crucial for quantum error correction, entanglement purification, and quantum repeaters, making it relevant to quantum communication and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of a minimal Kitaev chain device, resolving charge and parity dynamics relevant for Majorana qubits.
motivation: To enable fast and noninvasive readout of quantum dot-superconductor hybrid systems, which is crucial for realizing Majorana-based qubits and topological quantum computing.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry on a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal to probe charge and parity states.
result: They successfully resolve key processes and parity dynamics, demonstrating the viability of reflectometry for readout in such hybrid systems.
conclusion: This work provides a readout technique that can be integrated into Kitaev chain qubits, advancing the development of topological quantum computing.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method identifies the most strongly squeezed supermodes in multimode squeezed light, enabling compression of photonic processors from quadratic to near-constant hardware footprint.
motivation: Multimode squeezed light is a key resource for quantum information processing, but processing it typically requires hardware that scales quadratically with the number of modes. This work aims to reduce that overhead.
method: The authors use a variational approach to find the supermodes (linear combinations of original modes) that carry the most squeezing, effectively compressing the relevant information into fewer modes.
result: They demonstrate that the number of required processing modes can be reduced from quadratic to near-constant, significantly lowering hardware complexity.
conclusion: This variational compression technique could enable scalable quantum photonic processors and has implications for quantum communication and sensing.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, and Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020308] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control via shared lines incurs only logarithmic overhead, making it efficient for scaling quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires many control lines, which is challenging. The authors investigate whether time-multiplexed control (sharing lines) introduces significant overhead.
method: The authors analyze the overhead in terms of circuit depth and gate fidelity for various qubit topologies, using analytical and numerical methods to model serialization costs.
result: Serialization costs scale only logarithmically with the number of qubits, and for certain two-qubit gate configurations, there is no overhead at all.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable path for scaling quantum processors without prohibitive overhead, with implications for quantum computer architecture and control electronics.

title: High-Fidelity Controlled-Phase Gate For Binomial Codes Via Geometric Phase Engineering
authors: Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Lida Sun, Hongwei Huang, Zi-Jie Chen, Lintao Xiao, Bo Zhang, Chuanlong Ma, Ziyue Hua, Weiting Wang, Guangming Xue, Haifeng Yu, Weizhou Cai, Chang-Ling Zou, And Luyan Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Lida Sun, Hongwei Huang, Zi-Jie Chen, Lintao Xiao, Bo Zhang, Chuanlong Ma, Ziyue Hua, Weiting Wang, Guangming Xue, Haifeng Yu, Weizhou Cai, Chang-Ling Zou, and Luyan Sun

High-fidelity two-logical-qubit gates are essential for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation with bosonic codes, yet experimentally reported fidelities have rarely exceeded 90%. Here, we propose a geometric phase engineering approach for implementing controlled-phase gates for binomially enc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210602] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric phase engineering method to implement high-fidelity controlled-phase gates for binomial bosonic codes, achieving fidelities exceeding 99% in simulation.
motivation: High-fidelity two-logical-qubit gates are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation with bosonic codes, but experimental fidelities have been low.
method: Geometric phase engineering using a transmon qubit dispersively coupled to a cavity, where the gate is realized by adiabatic loops in phase space that accumulate geometric phases conditional on the logical states.
result: Simulated gate fidelities above 99% for binomial codes with up to four photons, and robustness against certain errors.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising path to high-fidelity logical gates for bosonic codes, with potential for experimental realization in superconducting circuits.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery to integrate two QEC codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computation requires non-Clifford gates, which are typically resource-intensive due to distillation. This work aims to reduce overhead by eliminating distillation.
method: Generalized lattice surgery is used to combine two quantum error-correcting codes, enabling the direct implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level without state distillation.
result: The scheme achieves fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates with reduced resource overhead compared to traditional distillation-based methods.
conclusion: This approach simplifies the path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation and may be integrated with quantum communication protocols that require logical gate operations.

title: Heisenberg-limited Two-parameter Estimation With Weighted Three-mode Schrödinger Cat States In A Triple-well Bose-Einstein Condensate System
authors: Cong Wang, Wei Shan, Jun-Qiao Pan, And Hai-Jun Xing
abstract:
Author(s): Cong Wang, Wei Shan, Jun-Qiao Pan, and Hai-Jun Xing

High-precision multiparameter estimation is critical in quantum metrology studies, where the precision (cost function) is expressed as a weighted sum of the covariances of the vector estimator. It necessitates the preparation of different input states to achieve optimal precision with varying weight…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062606] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Heisenberg-limited two-parameter estimation using weighted three-mode Schrödinger cat states in a triple-well Bose-Einstein condensate system.
motivation: High-precision multiparameter estimation is crucial for quantum metrology, and achieving optimal precision with weighted cost functions requires tailored input states.
method: The authors propose weighted three-mode Schrödinger cat states in a triple-well BEC and analyze their sensitivity for two-parameter estimation using quantum Fisher information matrix.
result: The weighted cat states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for both parameters simultaneously, outperforming unweighted states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical scheme for multiparameter estimation in BEC systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Dipolar-induced Rabi Dynamics And Trapping Of Chiral Magnons In Antiferromagnets
authors: Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, And Chenglong Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, and Chenglong Jia

Chiral magnons offer a promising platform for low-dissipation information processing, but efficient control of their internal degrees of freedom remains a big challenge. Here we demonstrate that dipolar interactions provide an intrinsic mechanism for coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferro…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220402] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Dipolar interactions enable coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferromagnets, offering a mechanism for low-dissipation information processing.
motivation: Chiral magnons are promising for low-dissipation information processing, but efficient control of their chirality remains challenging. This work aims to demonstrate that dipolar interactions can provide intrinsic coherent control.
method: The authors theoretically study dipolar-induced Rabi dynamics in antiferromagnets, using analytical and numerical methods to model the coupling between magnon modes and the resulting chirality dynamics.
result: Dipolar interactions drive Rabi oscillations between magnon modes of opposite chirality, enabling coherent control and trapping of chiral magnons.
conclusion: This work establishes dipolar interactions as a tool for coherent magnon chirality control, with implications for spintronic and magnonic devices. Future work may explore experimental realization and integration with quantum systems.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrating superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: To enable generation of complex non-Gaussian states for quantum sensing and error correction, which are important for quantum technologies.
method: The method uses trapped-ion systems with precise control over motional states via laser pulses, allowing the synthesis of arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states.
result: They experimentally realized superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, showing high fidelity and control.
conclusion: This work advances the ability to engineer quantum states in harmonic oscillators, with applications in quantum sensing, error correction, and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and optical manipulation. This work aims to overcome these limitations.
method: The authors couple circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: They achieve nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, preserving their quantum state.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, including potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
motivation: Simulating periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to learn effective Hamiltonians and dynamics efficiently.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators (FNOs) that operate in frequency space to capture temporal correlations, trained on data from time-periodic quantum systems to predict Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth.
result: FNOs accurately model the dynamics and generalize to unseen driving periods and system sizes, demonstrating faithful extrapolation and physical consistency.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful machine learning tool for studying Floquet systems, with potential applications in quantum control and understanding thermalization.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus and noise-induced concentration of loss functions, hindering trainability. Understanding the interplay between noise and expressivity is crucial for optimizing training.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the concentration of loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating the variance of the loss to the circuit's expressivity and noise level.
result: They show that noise can both help and hinder training: while it reduces expressivity, it also bounds the variance of the loss, potentially alleviating barren plateaus. The concentration rate depends on the circuit's effective dimension.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability, with implications for near-term quantum computing.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required to generate pseudorandom unitaries, showing that extensive doping is necessary.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of generating pseudorandom quantum states and unitaries is crucial for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments. The Clifford+T gate set is a common fault-tolerant basis, and non-Clifford gates are the expensive resource.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including entropy accumulation and properties of stabilizer states, to derive lower bounds on the number of T gates needed to achieve approximate unitary designs.
result: They prove that to generate an approximate unitary 2-design on n qubits, one needs at least Ω(n) non-Clifford gates, and for higher-order designs the scaling is polynomial in n. This shows that extensive doping is necessary.
conclusion: The results imply that random circuit sampling experiments and quantum supremacy demonstrations require a significant overhead of non-Clifford resources, which has implications for the feasibility of near-term quantum advantage and for the design of quantum algorithms.

title: Optimal Coherent Quantum Phase Estimation Via Tapering
authors: Dhrumil Patel, Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Yiğit Subaşı, And Andrew T. Sornborger
abstract:
Author(s): Dhrumil Patel, Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Yiğit Subaşı, and Andrew T. Sornborger

Leveraging optimal tapering functions from classical signal processing, coherent quantum phase estimation is shown to attain optimal performance with significantly reduced ancilla overhead.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020302] Published Thu Apr 02, 2026.
tldr: Coherent quantum phase estimation achieves optimal performance with reduced ancilla overhead by leveraging classical tapering functions.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but standard approaches require many ancilla qubits. This work aims to reduce resource requirements while maintaining optimal performance.
method: The authors apply optimal tapering functions from classical signal processing to coherent quantum phase estimation, analyzing the trade-off between ancilla count and estimation accuracy.
result: They demonstrate that tapering allows optimal phase estimation with significantly fewer ancilla qubits compared to conventional methods, without sacrificing precision.
conclusion: This work provides a practical resource reduction for quantum phase estimation, which could benefit near-term quantum algorithms and quantum communication protocols that rely on phase estimation.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, unifying various approaches across physics subfields.
motivation: Open quantum systems are central to quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The paper provides a Colloquium-style review, organizing different time-propagation techniques within a common framework and comparing their applicability.
result: It highlights commonalities and differences among methods used in quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, solid-state physics, and chemical physics.
conclusion: The review serves as a valuable resource for researchers to select appropriate simulation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems, with implications for quantum technologies and thermodynamics.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review examines how massive quantum systems can probe gravitational effects, including tests of gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement, which may inform quantum foundations.
motivation: Classical gravity is poorly tested at quantum scales; massive quantum systems offer a platform to study gravity's effect on quantum coherence and entanglement.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (e.g., gravity-induced decoherence, entanglement mediation) and experimental approaches using optomechanics, atom interferometry, and levitated particles.
result: Key findings include that experiments are approaching sensitivity to test whether gravity causes wavefunction collapse or mediates entanglement, with implications for quantum gravity.
conclusion: The results will guide theoretical descriptions of gravity on laboratory scales and may reveal nonclassical features of gravity, impacting quantum foundations and information thermodynamics.

title: Slow-light-enhanced Photon Drag In A Tunneling-coupled Quantum-dot System
authors: Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, And Zareen A. Khan
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, and Zareen A. Khan

We present a theoretical study of enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag within a four-level quantum-dot setup under the effect of dual interdot tunneling. Using the density-matrix formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field cond…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063709] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies slow-light-enhanced photon drag in a tunneling-coupled quantum-dot system, focusing on optical properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore enhanced photon drag effects in quantum-dot systems for potential applications in optical devices.
method: Theoretical analysis using density-matrix formalism to derive susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field conditions.
result: Enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag due to dual interdot tunneling and slow-light effects.
conclusion: The findings may be relevant for optical switching and sensing, but not directly for the user's research interests.

title: Graph-theoretic Quantum Contextuality And Unextendible Product Bases
authors: Gurvir Singh And Arvind
abstract:
Author(s): Gurvir Singh and Arvind

Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are central to the study of local distinguishability of orthogonal product states. While their connection to quantum nonlocality via Bell inequalities is well established, their link to quantum contextuality remains largely unexplored. We establish a graph theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062409] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a graph-theoretic connection between unextendible product bases and quantum contextuality, but does not directly address the user's specific interests in information thermodynamics, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
