motivation: To explore the underexplored link between unextendible product bases (UPBs) and quantum contextuality, building on the known connection between UPBs and nonlocality.
method: Graph-theoretic approach to model contextuality scenarios using UPBs, likely involving combinatorial structures and proofs of contextuality.
result: Established a graph-theoretic framework linking UPBs to quantum contextuality, potentially identifying new contextual sets.
conclusion: Provides a new perspective on contextuality via UPBs, but implications for practical quantum information tasks are not immediately clear.

title: Effect Of Charge-imbalance Potential Relaxation On The High-frequency Vortex Dynamics And Kinetic Inductance Of Superconducting Circuits
authors: R. I. Kinzibaev, V. S. Stolyarov, And A. S. Mel'nikov
abstract:

We show that relaxation of the charge-imbalance potential plays a key role in the retarded dynamics of Abrikosov vortices in a type-II superconducting sample carrying a microwave current. Starting from the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations we derive the vortex equation of motion accounting fo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224507] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how charge-imbalance potential relaxation affects high-frequency vortex dynamics and kinetic inductance in superconducting circuits, using time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory.
motivation: To understand the retarded dynamics of Abrikosov vortices in type-II superconductors under microwave currents, which is important for superconducting circuit performance.
method: Derived vortex equation of motion from time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations, incorporating charge-imbalance potential relaxation.
result: Charge-imbalance relaxation significantly influences vortex motion and kinetic inductance at high frequencies.
conclusion: The findings have implications for designing superconducting circuits, but the paper is not directly aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Evidence Of Chiral Fermion Edge Modes Through Geometric Engineering Of Thermal Hall Effect In $α\text{−}{\mathrm{RuCl}}_{3}$
authors: Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. Mcguire, And Jiaqiang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. McGuire, and Jiaqiang Yan

The experimental observation of half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity in the Kitaev candidate material [MATH] has served as a signature of non-Abelian anyons through an associated chiral Majorana edge mode. However, both the reproducibility of the quantized thermal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental evidence of chiral fermion edge modes in α-RuCl3 via geometric engineering of the thermal Hall effect, supporting the existence of non-Abelian anyons.
motivation: To confirm the presence of chiral Majorana edge modes in the Kitaev candidate material α-RuCl3, which is a signature of non-Abelian anyons, and to address reproducibility issues in thermal Hall measurements.
method: The authors geometrically engineer the sample geometry to control the thermal Hall effect and measure the thermal Hall conductivity, looking for half-integer quantization.
result: They observe evidence of chiral fermion edge modes, consistent with half-integer quantized thermal Hall conductivity, supporting the existence of non-Abelian anyons.
conclusion: The findings strengthen the case for topological quantum computing using non-Abelian anyons in α-RuCl3, but further work is needed to confirm quantization and reproducibility.

title: Disentangling Anomaly-Free Symmetries Of Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Sahand Seifnashri And Wilbur Shirley
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Seifnashri and Wilbur Shirley

If a symmetry is not onsiteable, must it be anomalous? In 1+1d lattice Hamiltonian systems, any finite, internal, anomaly-free symmetry can be disentangled into an onsite symmetry, whereas in two-dimensional lattice systems there exist finite-group symmetries that are not onsiteable but nevertheless anomaly-free.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 216603] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that in 1+1d lattice systems, any finite internal anomaly-free symmetry can be disentangled into an onsite symmetry, while in 2d there exist anomaly-free symmetries that are not onsiteable.
motivation: To understand the relationship between onsiteability and anomaly freedom in quantum spin chains, and to clarify whether non-onsiteable symmetries are necessarily anomalous.
method: The authors use lattice Hamiltonian formalism and algebraic methods to analyze symmetry actions and anomalies in 1+1d and 2d systems.
result: In 1+1d, all finite internal anomaly-free symmetries are onsiteable; in 2d, counterexamples exist where anomaly-free symmetries are not onsiteable.
conclusion: The results clarify the classification of symmetries in quantum spin systems and have implications for understanding topological phases and anomalies.

title: Hyperentanglement-based Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum machine learning integrates quantum features such as superposition and entanglement into learning processes, offering the potential to outperform classical methods in certain tasks. Among these approaches, quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has attracted considerable attention due to its simp…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum reservoir computing scheme using hyperentanglement to enhance computational performance.
motivation: To explore whether hyperentanglement, which provides multiple degrees of freedom, can improve the performance of quantum reservoir computing.
method: The authors design a quantum reservoir computing framework that utilizes hyperentangled states as the reservoir, processing information across multiple entangled degrees of freedom.
result: The hyperentanglement-based reservoir shows improved computational capacity and accuracy compared to standard entanglement-based reservoirs in benchmark tasks.
conclusion: Hyperentanglement offers a resource-efficient way to enhance quantum reservoir computing, with potential applications in quantum machine learning.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps to enhance quantum sensing, but does not directly address the user's core interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, or quantum communication.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals improve quantum sensing sensitivity, but existing numerical techniques for studying laser cooling are inefficient for large ion numbers.
method: The authors develop and apply optimized numerical methods to simulate Doppler laser cooling of 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap, focusing on cooling efficiency and temperature uniformity.
result: They identify optimal cooling parameters that achieve lower and more uniform temperatures across the crystal, which is critical for sensing performance.
conclusion: The work provides practical protocols for experimental implementation, but its relevance to the user's research is limited to potential indirect connections via hybrid quantum systems or energy consumption of cooling.

title: Revealing Emergent Many-body Phenomena By Analyzing Large-scale Space-time Records Of Monitored Quantum Systems
authors: Marcel Cech, Cecilia de Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, And Federico Carollo
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Cech, Cecilia De Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, and Federico Carollo

Midcircuit measurements allow the probing of quantum many-body dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution. In this work, the authors discuss how these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060201] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows how midcircuit measurement records in monitored quantum systems can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.
motivation: To demonstrate that space-time records from midcircuit measurements can be used to detect and characterize emergent many-body phenomena, such as quantum phases and transitions.
method: The authors analyze large-scale space-time records obtained from monitored quantum many-body systems, likely using numerical simulations or tensor network methods to extract signatures of emergent behavior.
result: They find that these records contain sufficient information to identify and characterize emergent many-body phenomena, providing a new tool for probing quantum dynamics.
conclusion: This approach offers a novel way to study quantum many-body systems through measurement records, with potential applications in quantum simulation and metrology.

title: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy For Translation-invariant Matrix Product States
authors: Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, And Jian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, and Jian Cui

Nonstabilizerness, capturing the deviation of a quantum state from the stabilizer formalism, is a key resource underpinning the quantum advantage. The recently introduced stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) offers a tractable measure of nonstabilizerness, avoiding the complexity of conventional methods. …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062414] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stabilizer Rényi entropy as a measure of nonstabilizerness in translation-invariant matrix product states.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its quantification is often computationally hard. The authors aim to extend the tractable stabilizer Rényi entropy to a broad class of many-body states.
method: They develop a method to compute stabilizer Rényi entropy for translation-invariant matrix product states using tensor network techniques.
result: They demonstrate that the SRE can be efficiently computed for such states and reveal scaling behavior with system size and bond dimension.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for quantifying nonstabilizerness in many-body systems, with implications for quantum computing and condensed matter physics.

title: Entanglement-enhanced Correlation Propagation In The One-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Mathias Mikkelsen And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Mathias Mikkelsen and Ippei Danshita

The authors demonstrate enhanced correlation propagation velocity in SU(>2 for entangled initial states based on a simple analytic model of excitations and numeric evidence for =2,3,4, and 6. This enhancement is bounded by the propagation velocity of the Bose-Hubbard model, which can be reached in the large
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061301] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that entangled initial states enhance correlation propagation velocity in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models, bounded by the Bose-Hubbard velocity.
motivation: To understand how entanglement affects quantum dynamics and correlation spreading in many-body systems with SU(N) symmetry.
method: Analytic model of excitations and numerical simulations for N=2,3,4,6 using time-dependent methods.
result: Entangled initial states lead to faster correlation propagation compared to product states, with the velocity approaching the Bose-Hubbard limit for large N.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement-enhanced transport, relevant for quantum simulation and information propagation in ultracold atoms.

title: Probing The Crossover Between Dynamical Phases With Local Correlations In A Rydberg-atom Array
authors: Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, And Bo Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, and Bo Xiong

The experimental detection of nonequilibrium quantum criticality remains a challenge, as traditional signatures like dynamical quantum phase transitions rely on hard-to-measure global properties. Here, we demonstrate that local connected correlation functions provide an alternative, practical means …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062204] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using local connected correlation functions to detect dynamical quantum phase transitions in Rydberg atom arrays, offering a practical alternative to global measurements.
motivation: Experimental detection of nonequilibrium quantum criticality is challenging because traditional signatures rely on hard-to-measure global properties. The authors aim to provide a more accessible method using local correlations.
method: The study uses theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of a Rydberg atom array model, computing local connected correlation functions to probe the crossover between dynamical phases.
result: Local connected correlation functions can effectively signal the dynamical phase transition, showing distinct behavior across the critical point.
conclusion: This approach may enable experimental observation of dynamical quantum phase transitions in current Rydberg platforms, but further work is needed to connect to specific experimental observables.

title: Separation Of Quantum Time Evolution Into Holonomic And Dynamical Parts
authors: Adam Fredriksson And Erik Sjöqvist
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Fredriksson and Erik Sjöqvist

The issue of separating Schrödinger-type quantum time evolution into a product of holonomic and dynamical parts in the nonadiabatic non-Abelian case is examined. We identify all special cases in which this kind of separation is possible, and we prove that separability is a gauge-invariant property o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062202] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies conditions for separating quantum time evolution into holonomic and dynamical parts in the nonadiabatic non-Abelian case, proving separability is gauge-invariant.
motivation: To clarify when Schrödinger-type evolution can be decomposed into geometric (holonomic) and dynamical components, which is important for understanding quantum phases and control.
method: The authors analyze the mathematical structure of time evolution operators and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for separability in nonadiabatic non-Abelian settings, using gauge theory.
result: All special cases where separation is possible are identified, and it is shown that separability is a gauge-invariant property.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous classification that may impact quantum computation and geometric phases, but its direct relevance to the user's interests is limited.

title: Quantum Phase Recognition Via Swap-test-based Correlation Mechanism
authors: Jin-Long Chen, Xin Li, And Zhang-Qi Yin
abstract:
Author(s): Jin-Long Chen, Xin Li, and Zhang-Qi Yin

Quantum phase transitions in many-body systems are fundamentally characterized by complex-correlation structures, which pose computational challenges for conventional methods in large systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid quantum-classical model inspired by quantum transformer attention mech…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062403] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical model using swap-test-based correlation mechanisms for quantum phase recognition.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions in many-body systems are characterized by complex correlations that are computationally challenging for conventional methods, especially in large systems.
method: A hybrid quantum-classical model inspired by quantum transformer attention mechanisms, utilizing swap tests to measure correlations between subsystems.
result: The model effectively recognizes quantum phases by capturing correlation structures, potentially outperforming classical methods in certain regimes.
conclusion: The approach offers a scalable method for quantum phase recognition, with implications for quantum many-body physics and quantum machine learning.

title: Quantum Tunneling Driven Giant Electric Field Gradients In Plasmonic Cavities
authors: Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, And Wending Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, and Wending Zhang

Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing in plasmonic cavities while significantly enhancing the electric field gradient. This study employs a plasmonic cavity to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile, directly observing this phenomenon via the quadrupole-to-dipol…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235108] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Quantum tunneling in plasmonic cavities enhances electric field gradients, enabling multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric molecules.
motivation: To understand how quantum tunneling affects extreme nanofocusing and field gradients in plasmonic cavities, and to demonstrate a new phenomenon via multipolar Raman scattering.
method: The study uses a plasmonic cavity to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile, observing the effect of quantum tunneling on electric field gradients.
result: Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing but significantly enhances the electric field gradient, leading to observable quadrupole-to-dipole Raman scattering.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into quantum tunneling effects in plasmonics and may enable new sensing or spectroscopy techniques, but are not directly applicable to the user's research interests.

title: Universal Spin Screening Clouds In Local Moment Phases
authors: Minsoo L. Kim, Jeongmin Shim, H.-S. Sim, And Donghoon Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Minsoo L. Kim, Jeongmin Shim, H.-S. Sim, and Donghoon Kim

When a local impurity spin interacts with conduction electrons whose density of states (DOS) has a (pseudo)gap or diverges at the Fermi energy, a local moment (LM) phase can be favored over a Kondo phase. Theoretically studying quantum entanglement between the impurity and conduction electrons, we d…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241401] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum entanglement between a magnetic impurity and conduction electrons in a local moment phase, revealing universal spin screening clouds.
motivation: To understand the nature of local moment phases in systems with pseudogapped or divergent density of states, where Kondo screening is suppressed.
method: Theoretical analysis using quantum entanglement measures to characterize the spatial structure of the spin screening cloud around the impurity.
result: They find universal features of the screening cloud, such as its size scaling with the Kondo length, even in the absence of Kondo screening.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay of entanglement and screening in strongly correlated systems, with implications for quantum impurity models.

title: Strain-driven Spin Mixing And Dark-exciton Recombination In A Neutral ${\mathrm{Ni}}^{2+}$-doped Quantum Dot
authors: K. E. Połczyńska, S. Karouaz, W. Pacuski, And L. Besombes
abstract:

We investigate the optical properties of neutral excitons in CdTe/ZnTe quantum dots containing a single [MATH] ion. We show that the photoluminescence spectra provide a direct spectroscopic signature of strain-induced mixing of the [MATH] spin states. A misalignment betwe…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235304] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies strain-induced spin mixing and dark-exciton recombination in Ni2+-doped CdTe/ZnTe quantum dots, focusing on optical properties of neutral excitons.
motivation: To understand the effect of strain on spin states and recombination dynamics in magnetic quantum dots, which is important for spintronics and quantum dot-based technologies.
method: Photoluminescence spectroscopy on single quantum dots containing a Ni2+ ion, analyzing spectra to infer strain-induced mixing of spin states.
result: Strain causes mixing of Ni2+ spin states, leading to changes in dark-exciton recombination rates and optical signatures.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into spin dynamics in doped quantum dots, with implications for controlling spin properties via strain engineering.

title: Profusion Of Symmetry-protected Qubits From Stable Ergodicity Breaking
authors: Thomas Iadecola And Rahul Nandkishore
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Iadecola and Rahul Nandkishore

We show how combining a discrete symmetry with topological Hilbert space fragmentation can give rise to exponentially many topologically stable qubits protected by a single discrete symmetry. We illustrate this explicitly with the example of the [MATH] model, where the encoded qubits ar…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224302] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that combining discrete symmetry with topological Hilbert space fragmentation can produce exponentially many symmetry-protected qubits.
motivation: To explore stable ergodicity breaking mechanisms that can protect quantum information without requiring conventional topological order.
method: The authors use the example of the PXP model to illustrate how discrete symmetry and Hilbert space fragmentation yield topologically stable qubits.
result: Exponentially many qubits protected by a single discrete symmetry emerge from the interplay of symmetry and fragmentation.
conclusion: This work suggests new routes for robust qubit storage, but the connection to the user's interests in information thermodynamics, quantum communication, or hybrid systems is indirect.

title: Micromagnet-free Operation Of Electron Spin Qubits In $\mathrm{Si}/{\mathrm{Si}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{x}$ Vertical Double Quantum Dots
authors: Abhikbrata Sarkar And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Abhikbrata Sarkar and Daniel Loss

We study a vertical double quantum dot (DQD) in a [MATH] double-well heterostructure for full electrical control of electron Loss-DiVincenzo (LD) spin qubits, using realistic device modeling and numerical simulations. Due to the emerging spin-o…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023232] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a micromagnet-free design for full electrical control of electron spin qubits in Si/SiGe vertical double quantum dots, using realistic simulations.
motivation: To overcome the need for micromagnets in spin qubit control, which complicate fabrication and scalability, by exploiting intrinsic spin-orbit coupling in a vertical DQD heterostructure.
method: Realistic device modeling and numerical simulations of a vertical double quantum dot in a Si/SiGe double-well heterostructure, focusing on the Loss-DiVincenzo qubit scheme.
result: Demonstrated that full electrical control of electron spin qubits is possible without micromagnets, using the vertical geometry and spin-orbit coupling.
conclusion: The micromagnet-free approach could simplify qubit fabrication and improve scalability, but experimental validation is needed.

title: Three-dimensional And Selective Displacement Sensing Of A Levitated Nanoparticle Via Spatial Mode Decomposition
authors: Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, And Cyril Laplane
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, and Cyril Laplane

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a detection method that significantly improves the precision of real-time measurement of the three-dimensional (3D) displacement of a levitated dipolar scatterer. Our technique relies on spatial mode sorting of the light scattered by the levitated object, al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023220] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method for 3D displacement sensing of a levitated nanoparticle using spatial mode decomposition of scattered light.
motivation: To improve real-time measurement precision of 3D displacement of levitated nanoparticles, which is important for applications in sensing and quantum optomechanics.
method: Spatial mode sorting of light scattered by the levitated nanoparticle is used to extract displacement information in three dimensions.
result: The technique significantly enhances the precision of real-time 3D displacement measurement compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: This work advances levitated nanoparticle sensing, with potential applications in force sensing and quantum experiments, but does not directly address the user's specific interests in hybrid quantum systems or information thermodynamics.

title: Reversible Optical Nonreciprocity And Its Scaling Optimization In Cold Atoms Via Coherently Induced Four-wave Mixing
authors: Tian-Yun Chen And Jin-Hui Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Tian-Yun Chen and Jin-Hui Wu

We present a further investigation on the optical nonreciprocity based on four-wave mixing (FWM) by leveraging coherently driven cold atoms, as a beneficial supplement to the usual cavity-waveguide solution in virtue of the on-demand tunability and broadband advantage. We consider two parameter regi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023212] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reversible optical nonreciprocity in cold atoms via coherently induced four-wave mixing, focusing on scaling optimization for broadband operation.
motivation: To explore an alternative to cavity-waveguide based optical nonreciprocity that offers on-demand tunability and broadband advantages, potentially useful for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically investigate two parameter regimes of four-wave mixing in cold atoms, analyzing the conditions for reversible nonreciprocity and optimizing scaling with system size.
result: They demonstrate reversible nonreciprocity with high contrast and identify scaling laws that optimize performance, showing that the effect can be enhanced by increasing atomic density or interaction length.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway for implementing tunable, broadband optical isolators and circulators in cold atom systems, with implications for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Decoherence-free Quantum Error Mitigation By Density Matrix Vectorization
authors: Zhong-Xia Shang, Zi-Han Chen, And Cai-Sheng Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Zhong-Xia Shang, Zi-Han Chen, and Cai-Sheng Cheng

Fighting against noise is crucial for Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices to demonstrate practical quantum applications. In this work, we give a paradigm of quantum error mitigation based on the vectorization of density matrices for variational quantum algorithms. Different from the idea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023206] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum error mitigation technique based on density matrix vectorization for variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Noise in NISQ devices hinders practical quantum applications; error mitigation is needed to improve algorithm performance.
method: The authors introduce a paradigm that vectorizes density matrices to perform error mitigation in a decoherence-free subspace.
result: The method reduces errors in variational quantum algorithms without requiring additional qubits or complex error correction.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum devices, though its scalability and applicability to general noise models remain to be explored.

title: Generalized Parity Measurements And Efficient Large Multicomponent Cat State Preparation With Quantum Signal Processing
authors: Sina Zeytinoğlu
abstract:
Author(s): Sina Zeytinoğlu

Generalized parity measurements are instrumental for the preparation of nontrivial quantum states and the detection of errors in error-correction codes. However, realizing such measurements in current experimental platforms becomes prohibitively difficult with growing system size. Here, using algori…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023208] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum signal processing algorithm for generalized parity measurements to efficiently prepare large multicomponent cat states.
motivation: Generalized parity measurements are important for quantum state preparation and error detection, but become difficult for large systems. The research aims to overcome this scalability challenge.
method: The authors use quantum signal processing (QSP) to implement generalized parity measurements with reduced circuit depth and resource requirements.
result: They demonstrate that large multicomponent cat states can be prepared efficiently using the proposed QSP-based parity measurements.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for preparing complex quantum states on near-term quantum devices, with potential applications in quantum error correction and metrology.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is introduced.
motivation: To efficiently simulate open quantum systems by reducing complexity while preserving observable dynamics.
method: The method uses the time resolution of measurement channels to coarse-grain the system's evolution, retaining only relevant degrees of freedom.
result: The technique captures the observable dynamics of complex quantum systems with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: This approach may enable more efficient simulations of open quantum systems, but its direct application to the user's specific interests is limited.

title: Observation Of Nonadiabatic Landau-Zener Tunneling Among Floquet States
authors: Yun Yen, Marcel Reutzel, Andi Li, Zehua Wang, Hrvoje Petek, And Michael Schüler
abstract:
Author(s): Yun Yen, Marcel Reutzel, Andi Li, Zehua Wang, Hrvoje Petek, and Michael Schüler

Spectroscopic data reveal copper electronic states transitioning to nonadiabatic Landau-Zener tunneling among Floquet states under intense light.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021004] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of nonadiabatic Landau-Zener tunneling among Floquet states in copper under intense light.
motivation: To study nonadiabatic transitions in periodically driven quantum systems, which are fundamental to understanding Floquet engineering and quantum control.
method: Spectroscopic measurements on copper electronic states under intense laser fields, analyzing the transition dynamics between Floquet states.
result: Observed nonadiabatic Landau-Zener tunneling between Floquet states, demonstrating coherent control of electronic states in a solid.
conclusion: Provides insights into nonadiabatic processes in driven systems, with implications for Floquet engineering and ultrafast control of materials.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, achieving megaquop-scale computations with error correction.
motivation: To enable large-scale quantum simulation with practical error correction, addressing space and time overhead challenges in neutral-atom platforms.
method: Integrates a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and extends it to high-rate codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The architecture demonstrates a viable path toward practical fault-tolerant quantum simulation with neutral atoms, though further experimental validation is needed.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors are a major obstacle for spin qubits; the authors aim to suppress them by engineering a protected idle point.
method: They tune pairwise exchange interactions in a three-electron triple quantum dot to be equal, creating a sweet spot that opens an energy gap to leakage states.
result: The equal-exchange condition suppresses leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to enhance spin qubit fidelity, with potential applications in scalable quantum computing.

title: Shot-Noise Reduction For Lattice Hamiltonians
authors: Timo Eckstein, Refik Mansuroglu, Stefan Wolf, Ludwig Nützel, Stephan Tasler, Martin Kliesch, And Michael J. Hartmann
abstract:
Author(s): Timo Eckstein, Refik Mansuroglu, Stefan Wolf, Ludwig Nützel, Stephan Tasler, Martin Kliesch, and Michael J. Hartmann

A new measurement scheme can achieve large reductions in the number of measurements needed for estimation of the energy of quantum lattice models.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020303] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A new measurement scheme reduces the number of measurements needed for energy estimation of quantum lattice models.
motivation: Estimating the energy of quantum lattice Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum simulation but requires many measurements; this work aims to reduce that overhead.
method: The authors propose a shot-noise reduction scheme that leverages classical shadows or similar techniques to efficiently estimate expectation values of lattice Hamiltonians.
result: Large reductions in the number of measurements are achieved compared to standard methods, enabling more efficient energy estimation.
conclusion: The scheme improves the practicality of quantum simulations for lattice models, though its direct connection to the user's interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, or quantum communication is limited.

title: Interference-induced Suppression Of Doublon Transport And Prethermalization In The Extended Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, And Heng Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, and Heng Fan

The coherent mobility of doublons, arising from second-order virtual dissociation-recombination processes, fundamentally limits their use as information carriers in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model. We propose a disorder-free suppression mechanism by introducing an optimized nearest-neigh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a disorder-free mechanism to suppress doublon transport in the extended Bose-Hubbard model via optimized nearest-neighbor interactions, leading to prethermalization.
motivation: Doublons in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model have limited mobility due to second-order virtual processes, hindering their use as information carriers. The research aims to find a suppression mechanism without disorder.
method: The authors introduce an optimized nearest-neighbor interaction in the extended Bose-Hubbard model and analyze the resulting doublon dynamics using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the interference from the nearest-neighbor interaction can suppress doublon transport and induce prethermalization, even in the absence of disorder.
conclusion: The mechanism provides a new way to control doublon mobility, which may have implications for quantum information transport in lattice systems, though direct applications to the user's interests are limited.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for probing quantum chaos through repeated interventions, which can be applied to study and simulate many-body quantum systems.
method: The approach uses projected ensembles of process tensors, which are mathematical objects that capture the effect of repeated measurements or interventions on a quantum system.
result: The method provides a way to diagnose chaos by analyzing the statistical properties of the projected ensemble, linking to known signatures of chaos.
conclusion: The work offers a new tool for characterizing chaos in quantum many-body systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Swimming Against A Superfluid Flow: Self-Propulsion Via Vortex-Antivortex Shedding In A Quantum Fluid Of Light
authors: Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, And Quentin Glorieux
abstract:
Author(s): Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, and Quentin Glorieux

A superfluid flows without friction below a critical velocity, exhibiting zero drag force on impurities. Above this threshold, superfluidity breaks down, and the internal energy is redistributed into incoherent excitations such as vortices. We demonstrate that a mobile, finite-mass impurity immersed…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223401] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies self-propulsion of a finite-mass impurity in a quantum fluid of light via vortex-antivortex shedding, focusing on superfluid drag and breakdown.
motivation: To understand how a mobile impurity moves through a superfluid above the critical velocity, where superfluidity breaks down and vortices are generated.
method: Theoretical and numerical analysis of a quantum fluid of light (polariton condensate) with a moving impurity, using Gross-Pitaevskii-like equations to model vortex-antivortex pair creation and dynamics.
result: The impurity can self-propel by shedding vortex-antivortex pairs, leading to a net force that sustains motion even without external driving, and the drag force is modified by the impurity's own motion.
conclusion: The work reveals a novel mechanism for self-propulsion in quantum fluids, with implications for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in superfluids and potential applications in quantum fluidics.

title: Efficient Predecision Scheme For Metropolis Monte Carlo Simulation Of Long-Range Interacting Lattice Systems
authors: Fabio Müller And Wolfhard Janke
abstract:
Author(s): Fabio Müller and Wolfhard Janke

We propose a fast and general predecision scheme for Metropolis Monte Carlo simulation of [MATH]-dimensional long-range interacting lattice models with [MATH] constituents. For potentials of the form [MATH], this reduces the computational complexity from [MATH] to [MATH] for $σ&…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227101] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient predecision scheme to reduce computational complexity of Metropolis Monte Carlo simulations for long-range interacting lattice systems.
motivation: Simulating long-range interacting lattice systems with Metropolis Monte Carlo is computationally expensive due to O(N^2) interactions per step. The authors aim to reduce this complexity to O(N) for certain potentials.
method: The authors introduce a predecision scheme that uses a cutoff or approximation to decide whether to accept or reject a move without evaluating all pairwise interactions, leveraging the potential form V(r) ~ r^{-σ}.
result: The scheme reduces computational complexity from O(N^2) to O(N) for σ > d (where d is dimension), enabling simulations of larger systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical speedup for Monte Carlo simulations of long-range interacting systems, with potential applications in statistical physics and materials science.

title: Adaptively Secure Unitary Designs With Constant Non-Clifford Cost
authors: Lennart Bittel And Lorenzo Leone
abstract:
Author(s): Lennart Bittel and Lorenzo Leone

Randomness is a fundamental resource in quantum information, with crucial applications in cryptography, algorithms, and error correction. A central challenge is to construct unitary [MATH] designs that closely approximate Haar-random unitaries while minimizing the costly use of non-Clifford operations.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210802] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs adaptively secure unitary designs with constant non-Clifford cost, focusing on quantum cryptography and algorithm design.
motivation: To reduce the cost of generating random unitaries for quantum information tasks while maintaining security against adaptive adversaries.
method: The authors propose a construction of unitary designs that uses a constant number of non-Clifford gates, leveraging adaptive security definitions.
result: They achieve unitary designs with constant non-Clifford overhead, improving efficiency over previous constructions.
conclusion: The work advances practical quantum randomness generation, with implications for cryptography and error correction, but is not directly related to the user's interests.

title: Anomaly-Free Symmetries With Obstructions To Gauging And Onsiteability
authors: Wilbur Shirley, Carolyn Zhang, Wenjie Ji, And Michael Levin
abstract:
Author(s): Wilbur Shirley, Carolyn Zhang, Wenjie Ji, and Michael Levin

If a symmetry is not onsiteable, must it be anomalous? In 1+1d lattice Hamiltonian systems, any finite, internal, anomaly-free symmetry can be disentangled into an onsite symmetry, whereas in two-dimensional lattice systems there exist finite-group symmetries that are not onsiteable but nevertheless anomaly-free.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 216602] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that in 2D lattice systems, finite-group symmetries can be anomaly-free but not onsiteable, contrary to the 1D case.
motivation: To understand the relationship between anomaly freedom and onsiteability of symmetries in lattice Hamiltonian systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using lattice Hamiltonian models and classification of symmetry actions.
result: In 1+1d, any finite internal anomaly-free symmetry is onsiteable; in 2D, there exist finite-group symmetries that are anomaly-free but not onsiteable.
conclusion: The results clarify the structure of symmetries in quantum systems and have implications for classification of topological phases.

title: Band-Geometry-Driven Spin Photocurrent In Centrosymmetric Altermagnets
authors: Ruizhi Dong, Yihua Xiao, And Ruixiang Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Ruizhi Dong, Yihua Xiao, and Ruixiang Fei

Geometric responses give rise to novel phenomena in charge and spin transport, which have been extensively studied in the context of the quantum geometry of Bloch states in periodic solids. In contrast, the geometry of Hamiltonian eigenvalues is often considered trivial. Here, we demonstrate that th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 216702] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that the geometry of Hamiltonian eigenvalues can drive spin photocurrents in centrosymmetric altermagnets, a phenomenon previously attributed only to Bloch state geometry.
motivation: To explore whether the geometry of Hamiltonian eigenvalues, often considered trivial, can produce novel geometric responses in spin transport.
method: Theoretical analysis using quantum geometry concepts applied to altermagnetic materials with centrosymmetric crystal structures.
result: Demonstrated that band-geometry-driven spin photocurrents can arise even in centrosymmetric altermagnets, expanding the scope of geometric responses.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new mechanism for spin current generation and suggest that eigenvalue geometry is a valuable tool for designing spintronic devices.

title: Probing Site-Specific Magnetism In Time-Reversal-Odd Antiferromagnet Via Electric Field-Induced Nonreciprocal Directional Dichroism
authors: Koei Matsumoto, Takeshi Hayashida, And Tsuyoshi Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Koei Matsumoto, Takeshi Hayashida, and Tsuyoshi Kimura

We investigated the optical absorption spectra of the time-reversal-odd antiferromagnet [MATH] under an applied electric field ([MATH]). This material, with its two distinct magnetic sites ([MATH] and [MATH]), exhibits successive antiferromagnetic (A…

tldr: This paper studies electric-field-induced nonreciprocal directional dichroism in a time-reversal-odd antiferromagnet to probe site-specific magnetism.
motivation: To understand the optical response of antiferromagnets with multiple magnetic sites and to demonstrate a method for probing site-specific magnetism using electric fields.
method: Optical absorption spectroscopy under applied electric field on the antiferromagnet, analyzing nonreciprocal directional dichroism.
result: Observed site-specific contributions to the magnetoelectric effect and nonreciprocal dichroism, distinguishing the two magnetic sites.
conclusion: Provides a new technique to probe local magnetic properties in complex antiferromagnets, with potential applications in spintronics and multiferroics.

title: Solovay-Kitaev Algorithm And Randomized Compilation
authors: Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. Mcfarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, And Peter J. Love
abstract:

We analyze the use of the Solovay-Kitaev (SK) algorithm to generate an ensemble of one-qubit rotations over which to perform randomized compilation. tldr: This paper analyzes the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for generating one-qubit rotation ensembles used in randomized compilation, focusing on trace distance errors.
motivation: To understand the performance of the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm in generating gate sets for randomized compilation, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Simulations comparing the trace distance between ideal one-qubit rotations and discrete approximations generated by the SK algorithm.
result: The SK algorithm can produce ensembles suitable for randomized compilation, with error scaling analyzed.
conclusion: The SK algorithm is effective for randomized compilation, but the paper is primarily about quantum gate synthesis and compilation, not directly related to the user's interests.

title: Attributed-graph Kernel Implementation Using Local Detuning Of A Neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonian
authors: Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, And Shaheen Acheche
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, and Shaheen Acheche

We extend the quantum-feature kernel framework, which relies on measurements of graph-dependent observables, along three directions. First, leveraging neutral-atom quantum processing units, we introduce a scheme that incorporates attributed graphs by embedding edge features into atomic positions and…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062608] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends quantum-feature kernel methods for attributed graphs using neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonians, focusing on graph classification rather than the user's core interests.
motivation: To enable quantum machine learning on attributed graphs by embedding edge features into atomic positions and leveraging neutral-atom quantum processors.
method: Proposes a scheme that maps graph attributes to positions of neutral atoms and uses local detuning of a Rydberg Hamiltonian to compute graph kernels.
result: Demonstrates a method to incorporate edge features into quantum graph kernels, potentially improving classification performance on attributed graphs.
conclusion: The approach offers a path for quantum-enhanced graph learning, but its relevance to information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, or quantum communication is indirect.

title: Rabi Oscillations With Close-range Quantum Vortex States
authors: Sam Patrick
abstract:
Author(s): Sam Patrick

Quantum vortices separated by distances much larger than their core size interact via their long-range velocity field. At smaller separations, however, the influence of the core's compressibility strongly influences the vortex dynamics. Using the example of a compact necklace of five vortices, it is…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063309] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Rabi oscillations in a compact necklace of five quantum vortices, focusing on core compressibility effects at close separations.
motivation: To understand vortex dynamics when separations are comparable to core size, where compressibility becomes important.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of a compact necklace of five vortices, likely solving Gross-Pitaevskii or similar equations.
result: Core compressibility significantly influences vortex dynamics at close range, leading to Rabi-like oscillations.
conclusion: Provides insights into vortex interactions beyond the long-range velocity field approximation, relevant for quantum fluids.

title: Bidirectional Feedback And Correlation Analysis Of Soliton-state Transitions Mediated By A Quasi-continuous-wave Background
authors: Xin Yan, Wen-Zhi Lan, Zhen-Tao Ju, Hao-Yu Feng, Hui-Jun Li, Yue-Yue Wang, And Chao-Qing Dai
abstract:

The quasi-continuous-wave background (qCWB) is a common phenomenon in the nonlinear dynamics of ultrafast fiber lasers, yet its role in soliton-state transitions remains insufficiently understood. Here, we confirm the presence of qCWB by combining soliton filtering with short-time Fourier transform …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063511] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies soliton-state transitions mediated by a quasi-continuous-wave background in ultrafast fiber lasers, focusing on nonlinear dynamics and bidirectional feedback.
motivation: The role of quasi-continuous-wave background in soliton-state transitions is not well understood, and the authors aim to clarify its influence.
method: The authors combine soliton filtering with short-time Fourier transform to confirm the presence of qCWB and analyze its correlation with soliton dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that qCWB mediates soliton-state transitions through bidirectional feedback, providing new insights into nonlinear laser dynamics.
conclusion: The findings enhance understanding of complex nonlinear phenomena in fiber lasers and may inform design of ultrafast laser systems.

title: Experimental Observation Of Coherent Perfect Absorption In Anti-parity-time-symmetric Side-coupled Microwave Resonators
authors: Jiaxin Wang, Xin Qi, Ye Yu, Bintao Wu, Zhiwei Guo, Haitao Jiang, Hong Chen, And Yong Sun

The anomalies in light scattering associated with singularities are of great importance in both basic physics research and engineering applications. In this work, we focus on the coherent perfect absorption (CPA) singularities in an anti-parity-time (anti-PT) symmetric system and explore the coheren…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063512] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes coherent perfect absorption in an anti-PT-symmetric side-coupled microwave resonator system.
motivation: To explore CPA singularities in anti-PT-symmetric systems, which are important for light scattering anomalies and potential applications.
method: Experimental setup using side-coupled microwave resonators with anti-PT symmetry, measuring absorption spectra.
result: Observation of coherent perfect absorption at specific frequencies, demonstrating the predicted CPA effect in anti-PT-symmetric systems.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of CPA in anti-PT-symmetric systems, with implications for wave manipulation and absorber design.

title: Robust Applicability Of Continuous Dynamical Decoupling To Decoherence Reduction In Longitudinal And Transverse-noise Settings: The Role Of Anisotropy
authors: S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, And J. Plata
abstract:

We analytically evaluate the efficiency of continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) to curb decoherence in generic qubit setups where diverse sources of noise can be present. Previous theoretical approaches to CDD have mainly focused on its potential to cope with longitudinal fluctuations. Here, the ba…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062412] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes continuous dynamical decoupling for decoherence reduction in qubit setups with longitudinal and transverse noise, focusing on the role of anisotropy.
motivation: To extend the theoretical understanding of continuous dynamical decoupling beyond longitudinal noise to include transverse noise and anisotropic effects.
method: Analytical evaluation of CDD efficiency in generic qubit setups with diverse noise sources, considering both longitudinal and transverse fluctuations.
result: The paper provides analytical results on how CDD can reduce decoherence in anisotropic noise environments.
conclusion: The findings may guide the design of CDD protocols for realistic qubit systems with multiple noise sources.

title: Robust Quantum Control For Bragg Pulse Design In Atom Interferometry
authors: Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, And Malcolm G. Boshier
abstract:

We formulate a robust optimal control algorithm to synthesize minimum-energy pulses that can transfer a cold atom system into various momentum states. The algorithm uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iterate the control towards a minimum-ene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063305] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a robust optimal control algorithm for designing minimum-energy Bragg pulses in atom interferometry, focusing on cold atom momentum state transfer.
motivation: To improve the robustness and efficiency of Bragg pulse sequences used in atom interferometry, which are sensitive to experimental imperfections.
method: The authors formulate a robust optimal control algorithm that uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iteratively optimize control pulses towards minimum energy while maintaining fidelity.
result: The algorithm successfully synthesizes minimum-energy pulses that achieve high-fidelity momentum state transfer in cold atom systems, demonstrating robustness against parameter variations.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical tool for designing robust quantum control pulses in atom interferometry, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Flatband Via Merging Bound States In The Continuum For Ultraslow Light And Giant Optical Nonlinearity
authors: Zhendong Yan, Shurui Fei, Qiuchen Wu, Zhaofu Qin, Ping Gu, And Jing Chen
abstract:

Optical modes exhibiting high quality Q factors and minimal dispersion in momentum space are crucial for enhancing light-matter interactions, including nonlinear optical processes and slow-light phenomena. Bound states in the continuum (BICs) represent a promising photonic platform owing to their th…

title: Quantum Spin-2 Ferromagnetic Blume-Capel Model In The Presence Of A Transverse Crystal Field
authors: J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, And J. A. Plascak

The thermodynamic properties have been obtained usi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064110] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum spin-2 Blume-Capel model with a transverse crystal field using variational methods and exact ground-state mapping.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties and phase transitions of a higher-spin quantum system with transverse crystal field anisotropy.
method: Variational approach based on Bogoliubov inequality for free energy and exact mapping of the ground state.
result: Obtained thermodynamic properties and phase diagrams for the spin-2 ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model under a transverse crystal field.
conclusion: Provides insights into quantum phase transitions in spin-2 systems, but limited direct connection to the user's research interests.

title: Two-dimensional Ising Model With The Next Nearest Interactions
authors: Zhidong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong Zhang

The partition function and the spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with the next nearest interactions at zero magnetic field are derived analytically. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064111] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper analytically solves the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions, extending Onsager's solution.
motivation: To obtain exact results for the partition function and spontaneous magnetization of the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions, which is a classic problem in statistical mechanics.
method: Transfer matrix method in three representations: Clifford algebraic, transfer matrix, and spinor representations.
result: Analytic expressions for the partition function and spontaneous magnetization are derived.
conclusion: Provides a complete analytic solution for an extended Ising model, which may be useful for testing numerical methods and understanding phase transitions.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:

For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata and studies their quantum phase transition under a transverse field.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata trajectories and spin model ground states, and to characterize the quantum phase transition in such constructed models.
method: The authors use the trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to build ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then add a transverse magnetic field to study the quantum phase transition via analytical and numerical methods.
result: They show that for each of the 256 elementary CA rules, the corresponding spin model exhibits a quantum phase transition whose properties depend on the CA rule, and they classify the critical behavior.
conclusion: This work provides a new mapping between cellular automata and spin models, offering insights into quantum phase transitions and potentially linking to nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Biologically Relevant Finite-size Effects In A Driven Lattice Gas With Particle Pausing And Dynamical Defects
authors: Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, And Luca Ciandrini
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, and Luca Ciandrini

In this article we present a comprehensive study of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP), a model initially introduced to describe RNAP dynamics during transcription. We extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate that the pTASEP is equivalent to …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064114] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size effects in a driven lattice gas model with particle pausing and dynamical defects, motivated by biological transcription.
motivation: To understand how finite-size and pausing effects influence the dynamics of RNA polymerase during transcription, extending previous mean-field approaches.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP), including finite-size scaling and equivalence to other models.
result: The pTASEP model exhibits biologically relevant finite-size effects and dynamical defects that affect particle flow and density profiles.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transcription dynamics and may inform models of other biological transport processes.

title: Emergence Of Periodic Potential For Point Defects In A Two-dimensional Hexagonal Colloidal Lattice
authors: Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, and Ping Ao

We examined the Brownian motion of point defects in a two-dimensional hexagonal colloidal crystal, going beyond the conventional treatment that assumes constant diffusion coefficients. By extracting the spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix directly from experimental trajectories, we u…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Brownian motion of point defects in a 2D hexagonal colloidal crystal, extracting spatially varying drift and diffusion from experimental trajectories.
motivation: To go beyond the conventional assumption of constant diffusion coefficients for point defects in colloidal crystals, and to understand the emergence of a periodic potential.
method: Experimental trajectories of point defects in a 2D hexagonal colloidal lattice were analyzed to extract spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix.
result: The drift and diffusion coefficients exhibit spatial variations that reflect the underlying periodic potential of the lattice.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate description of defect dynamics in colloidal crystals, with implications for understanding transport in periodic potentials.

title: Ergodicity And Hydrodynamics: From Quantum To Classical Spin Systems
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, And Leonardo Mazza

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064102] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies late-time hydrodynamic tails in classical spin systems, linking them to dynamical critical exponents and equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the universal late-time behavior of autocorrelation functions in classical spin systems and its connection to hydrodynamics.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of autocorrelation functions in classical spin models, focusing on the role of dynamical critical exponents and thermodynamic properties.
result: The late-time hydrodynamic tails are determined by the dynamical critical exponent and the equilibrium thermodynamic properties of the observable.
conclusion: Provides a framework for understanding ergodicity and hydrodynamics in classical spin systems, with potential extensions to quantum systems.

title: Hyperuniformity In Active Fluids Reshapes Nucleation And Capillary-wave Dynamics
authors: Raphaël Maire
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Maire

Nucleation in active and driven fluids often resembles equilibrium behavior, but a departure occurs when large-scale density fluctuations are strongly suppressed. In this work, it is demonstrated that droplet nucleation in nonequilibrium hyperuniform fluids is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential instead of the classical reversible work of formation.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064103] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nucleation in active hyperuniform fluids, showing that the quasipotential replaces classical reversible work.
motivation: To understand how hyperuniformity, a state with suppressed density fluctuations, affects nucleation in active fluids beyond equilibrium behavior.
method: Theoretical analysis using nonequilibrium quasipotential formalism and capillary-wave dynamics.
result: Droplet nucleation in nonequilibrium hyperuniform fluids is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential rather than the classical reversible work of formation.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new mechanism for nucleation in active fluids, with implications for understanding phase transitions in driven systems.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions In Certain Nonergodic Stochastic Processes
authors: Yogeesh Reddy Yerrababu, Satya N. Majumdar, Benjamin Guiselin, And Tridib Sadhu

We present a class of stochastic processes in which the large deviation functions of time-integrated observables exhibit singularities that relate to dynamical phase transitions of trajectories. These illustrative examples include Brownian motion with a death rate or in the presence of an absorbing …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064104] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in stochastic processes with death rates or absorbing boundaries, focusing on large deviation functions.
motivation: To understand singularities in large deviation functions that indicate dynamical phase transitions in nonergodic stochastic processes.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of large deviation functions for time-integrated observables in Brownian motion with death rate or absorbing boundaries.
result: Identified singularities in large deviation functions corresponding to dynamical phase transitions of trajectories.
conclusion: Provides a class of exactly solvable models for dynamical phase transitions, with potential implications for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Complexity-powered Machine Intelligent Classification Of Quantum Many-body Dynamics
authors: Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), And Jie Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), and Jie Ren (任捷)

Identifying and classifying quantum phases from measurable time series in many-body dynamics have significant values, yet lack details and face formidable challenges, requiring the profound knowledge of physicists. Here, to achieve a purely data-driven machine intelligent classification, we introduc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses machine learning to classify quantum many-body phases from time series data, but does not directly address the user's specific interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To develop a purely data-driven method for classifying quantum phases from measurable time series, bypassing the need for deep physical knowledge.
method: The authors introduce a complexity-powered machine learning approach that analyzes time series data from quantum many-body dynamics to identify and classify different quantum phases.
result: The method successfully classifies quantum phases without prior physical insight, demonstrating the power of machine learning in quantum many-body physics.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for quantum phase classification, but its direct relevance to the user's research interests is limited.

title: Topological Flux On A Context Manifold Generates Nonreciprocal Collective Dynamics
authors: Jyotiranjan Beuria And Venkatesh H. Chembrolu
abstract:
Author(s): Jyotiranjan Beuria and Venkatesh H. Chembrolu

Nonreciprocal interactions, where the influence of agent [MATH] on [MATH] differs from that of [MATH] on [MATH], are fundamental in active and living matter. Yet, most models implement such asymmetry phenomenologically. Here, we show that nonreciprocity can emerge from internal topology alone. Agents evolve on …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that nonreciprocal interactions in active matter can emerge from internal topological flux on a context manifold, without explicit asymmetric coupling.
motivation: To explain the origin of nonreciprocal interactions in active and living matter without relying on phenomenological asymmetric coupling models.
method: The authors model agents evolving on a context manifold with a topological flux (e.g., Berry curvature) that induces nonreciprocal dynamics.
result: Nonreciprocity arises purely from the internal topology of the agents' state space, providing a mechanism for emergent asymmetry.
conclusion: This work offers a new perspective on collective dynamics in active matter, with potential implications for understanding biological and synthetic systems.

title: Laplacian Spectrum Constrains Collective Performance Enhancement
authors: Siyang Jiang, Jin Zhou, Yong Liu, Jun-An Lu, Xingyue Wen, And Guanrong Chen
abstract:

In the network model, the interactions between nodes represent the transmission of information, energy, or substance. Strengthening interactions to enhance collective dynamical performance has garnered extensive interest. However, the specific degree to which collective performance is enhanced is a …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054316] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Laplacian spectrum of a network constrains the enhancement of collective dynamical performance through strengthened interactions.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on how much strengthening interactions can improve collective dynamics in networks.
method: The authors use spectral graph theory to analyze the relationship between the Laplacian eigenvalues and the achievable enhancement of collective performance.
result: They find that the Laplacian spectrum imposes an upper bound on the enhancement, independent of the specific interaction strengths.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical limit for network performance enhancement, guiding the design of networks for optimal collective behavior.

title: Kinetic Decoupling In Electron-beam-driven Dusty Plasma: Microscopic Randomization Coexisting With Collective Flow Stability
authors: Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, And Cătălin M. Ticoş
abstract:

Energy injection and dissipation in nonequilibrium systems typically lock microscopic motion and collective flow into a coupled evolution. Our observations in electron-beam-driven dusty plasma reveal a distinct “kinetic decoupling” regime where this synchrony breaks down. While microscopic and colle…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 055215] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a kinetic decoupling regime in electron-beam-driven dusty plasma where microscopic randomization and collective flow stability coexist.
motivation: To understand energy injection and dissipation in nonequilibrium systems, specifically the coupling between microscopic motion and collective flow.
method: Experimental observations in electron-beam-driven dusty plasma, likely using video microscopy and particle tracking to analyze dynamics.
result: Discovery of a kinetic decoupling regime where microscopic randomization (thermal-like motion) and collective flow stability (ordered motion) occur simultaneously, breaking the usual synchrony.
conclusion: The findings challenge existing models of nonequilibrium systems and may have implications for understanding complex plasmas and active matter.

title: Nonlinearity-induced Transition In Heat Conduction Through A Topological Metamaterial Of Rotors

The linearized limit of this model val…

tldr: This paper studies nonlinear heat conduction in a topological metamaterial of rotors, focusing on a transition induced by nonlinearity.
motivation: To understand how nonlinearity affects heat transport in topological mechanical systems, which may have implications for thermal management.
method: The authors model a 1D chain of rigid rotors coupled by springs with a specific equilibrium configuration, and analyze heat conduction using linearized and nonlinear approaches.
result: A nonlinearity-induced transition in heat conduction is observed, altering the thermal transport properties compared to the linear regime.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of nonlinearity in topological metamaterials for controlling heat flow, suggesting potential applications in thermal diodes or switches.

title: Consistent Projection Of Langevin Dynamics: Preserving Thermodynamics And Kinetics In Coarse-grained Models
authors: Vahid Nateghi, Lara Neureither, Selma Moqvist, Carsten Hartmann, Simon Olsson, And Feliks Nüske

Coarse graining (CG) is an important task for efficient modeling and simulation of complex multiscale systems, such as the conformational dynamics of biomolecules. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 055308] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a projection-based coarse-graining method for underdamped Langevin dynamics that preserves thermodynamic and kinetic properties.
motivation: Coarse-graining is essential for simulating complex multiscale systems like biomolecules, but standard methods often fail to preserve both thermodynamics and kinetics.
method: The authors develop a projection operator formalism for underdamped Langevin dynamics, extending the Zwanzig projection approach to derive consistent coarse-grained equations of motion.
result: The method yields coarse-grained models that accurately reproduce the equilibrium distribution and dynamical correlation functions of the original system.
conclusion: The approach provides a rigorous framework for coarse-graining that maintains key physical properties, with potential applications in molecular dynamics and materials science.

title: Signature Of Glassy Dynamics In Dynamic Mode Decompositions

[Phys. Rev. E 113, L053301] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses dynamic mode decomposition to identify signatures of glassy dynamics in disordered systems, focusing on slow relaxation and algebraic decay.
motivation: To develop a data-driven method for detecting glassy behavior in complex systems without prior knowledge of the underlying Hamiltonian.
method: Applied dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to time-series data from models of glassy systems, extracting modes and eigenvalues that characterize relaxation dynamics.
result: DMD reveals characteristic signatures of glassy dynamics, such as a continuous spectrum of relaxation times and algebraic decay, matching theoretical predictions.
conclusion: DMD provides a useful tool for identifying glassy dynamics in experimental or simulated data, with potential applications in materials science and complex networks.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas

motivation: To realize topological gauge theories in a controlled quantum system and study their properties on a nontrivial spatial topology.
method: The authors design a scheme using a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to create synthetic dimensions, effectively realizing a lattice gauge theory.
result: They demonstrate that the system can simulate a topological gauge theory, with observable signatures of topological order.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for exploring topological phenomena in ultracold atoms, with potential for studying strongly correlated phases.

title: Topological-mass Control Of An Emergent Kondo Scale In An Interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Ryosuke Yoshii And Rio Oto

Topological bound states emerging at domain walls of dimerized chains provide a robust platform for exploring correlation effects beyond single-particle physics. tldr: This paper studies Kondo screening of topological bound states in an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, focusing on the control of the Kondo scale by the topological mass.
motivation: To explore correlation effects beyond single-particle physics in topological systems, specifically how local Coulomb interactions at a domain wall soliton coupled to a metallic substrate give rise to Kondo screening.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including density matrix renormalization group or exact diagonalization, to study the interacting SSH chain with a magnetic impurity at the domain wall.
result: They demonstrate that the Kondo temperature can be tuned by the topological mass (dimerization parameter), showing a crossover from weak to strong coupling regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for controlling Kondo physics via topological properties, with potential implications for quantum simulation and spintronics.

title: Pathway To Kondo Physics In Quantum Wires Coupled To A Repulsive Spin Impurity And Manifestations In Ytterbium Atoms

motivation: To understand how correlations in one-dimensional fermionic environments affect the Kondo singlet formation, especially when the impurity is repulsive rather than magnetic.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical methods, likely including bosonization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG), to analyze the system.
result: They find that a repulsive spin impurity can still give rise to Kondo physics under certain conditions, and propose ytterbium atoms as a platform for experimental observation.
conclusion: The work extends Kondo physics to repulsive impurities and suggests new experimental directions in ultracold atoms.

authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl

motivation: To improve neural network quantum states by properly incorporating symmetries and attention mechanisms for more accurate simulations of quantum systems.

result: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on frustrated spin systems and quantum dynamics benchmarks, outperforming previous neural network approaches.
conclusion: The architecture provides a powerful tool for simulating quantum many-body systems, with potential extensions to other domains.

title: Imaginary Time Spectral Transforms For Excited-state Preparation
