motivation: To develop a method for preparing excited states in quantum many-body systems without explicit matrix inversion, which is computationally expensive.
method: Combines a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution, implemented via tensor-network simulations and compatible with hybrid quantum-classical platforms.
result: Demonstrated on disordered spin chains, showing effective preparation of excited eigenstates.
conclusion: The method offers a scalable approach for excited-state preparation, with potential applications in quantum simulation and hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.

title: Algorithmic Aspects Of Gauged Gaussian Fermionic Projected Entangled Pair States: Gauge Fixing And Translation Invariance
authors: Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, And Patrick Emonts

Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) provide a powerful framework for studying nonperturbative phenomena in gauge theories. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic techniques for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance in gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS), advancing tensor network methods for lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative physics, but conventional Monte Carlo methods suffer from sign problems and cannot handle real-time evolution. Tensor network methods like PEPS offer an alternative, but gauged fermionic PEPS require careful handling of gauge redundancy and symmetries.
method: The authors propose algorithmic procedures for gauge fixing in Gaussian fermionic PEPS with gauge symmetries, and for imposing translation invariance to reduce computational cost. They likely use matrix product state techniques and variational optimization.
result: The paper presents efficient gauge-fixing algorithms and demonstrates how to enforce translation invariance, enabling more scalable simulations of lattice gauge theories with fermionic matter.
conclusion: These algorithmic advances make gauged fermionic PEPS a more practical tool for studying lattice gauge theories, potentially enabling simulations of real-time dynamics and systems with sign problems.

title: Straintronics And Twistronics In Bilayer Graphene
authors: Federico Escudero, Dong Wang, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Shengjun Yuan, Francisco Guinea, And Zhen Zhan

tldr: This paper studies the interplay of twist and strain in bilayer graphene to engineer moiré patterns and narrow bands for correlated and topological phases.
motivation: To understand how strain, as an additional control knob, can modify the electronic properties of twisted bilayer graphene beyond the magic-angle condition.
method: Theoretical modeling and band structure calculations for strained and twisted bilayer graphene.
result: Strain can induce or modify moiré patterns and narrow bands, potentially hosting correlated and topological phases.
conclusion: Strain provides a realistic tuning parameter for band engineering in bilayer graphene, complementing twist angle control.

title: Evolving Disorder In non-Hermitian Lattices
authors: I. Komis, E. T. Kokkinakis, K. G. Makris, And E. N. Economou

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023227] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the impact of evolving disorder on wave transport in non-Hermitian lattices, revealing unique transport features distinct from static disorder.
motivation: While static disorder in non-Hermitian systems has been studied, the effects of time-varying (evolving) disorder remain largely unexplored, motivating this work.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in non-Hermitian lattices with disorder that evolves in time, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: Evolving disorder leads to peculiar transport phenomena such as jumpy wave evolution and can suppress or enhance localization depending on the disorder dynamics.
conclusion: The findings extend the understanding of disorder in non-Hermitian systems and may have implications for controlling wave transport in open systems.

title: Spinor Pairing Order Enforced By Berry Phase
authors: Yi Li And Grayson R. Frazier

motivation: To explore exotic superconducting phases that emerge from topological band structures, specifically pairing between bands with different Chern numbers.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological band theory and Berry phase concepts to construct the pairing order parameter and derive its consequences.
result: The pairing leads to a single Bogoliubov-Weyl node violating the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, protected gapless surface states, and a fractional Mermin-Ho relation for superfluid velocity.
conclusion: This work reveals a new class of topological superconductivity with potential implications for fault-tolerant quantum computing and understanding of topological matter.

title: Taxonomy Of Prediction
authors: Alexandra Jurgens And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandra Jurgens and James P. Crutchfield

A prediction makes a claim about a system's future given knowledge of its past. A retrodiction makes a claim about its past given knowledge of its future. tldr: The paper introduces the bidirectional machine, a hidden Markov model that optimally performs both prediction and retrodiction by encoding all statistical dependencies in its state structure.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for optimal prediction and retrodiction in stochastic processes, addressing the asymmetry between forward and backward inference.
method: The authors construct a bidirectional hidden Markov chain that captures both predictive and retrodictive information, leveraging computational mechanics and information theory.
result: The bidirectional machine achieves optimal performance for both prediction and retrodiction, revealing the minimal state complexity required for bidirectional inference.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for understanding temporal inference in complex systems, with potential applications in time series analysis and machine learning.

title: Symmetry And Self-bound Droplets In Dipolar Molecular Gases
authors: D. Baillie
abstract:
Author(s): D. Baillie

Recent experiments with degenerate molecular gases dressed by elliptically polarized microwave fields have enabled new control of dipolar interactions via engineered anisotropy. method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any photonic state into a sequence of operations that can be implemented with current experimental platforms.
result: They show that every photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic tools.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic approach to photonic state preparation, potentially advancing quantum computing and communication experiments.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant quantum computation of molecular energies using error-corrected logical qubits on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated into practical quantum chemistry simulations, improving accuracy despite hardware noise.
method: Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets were employed on a trapped-ion quantum processor to compute molecular energies.
result: The computation achieved improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum chemistry.
conclusion: The work paves the way for larger-scale error-corrected quantum simulations, though further improvements in logical gate fidelities are needed.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectral analysis.
motivation: To overcome worst-case complexity barriers in classical spectral analysis by leveraging quantum algorithms.
method: Quantum filtering techniques that estimate eigenvalue multiplicities and cluster locations.
result: The algorithm efficiently identifies clusters and multiplicities, offering advantages over classical methods.
conclusion: Provides a new quantum tool for spectral analysis with potential applications in quantum computing and numerical linear algebra.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops fault-tolerant protocols for Majorana-based quantum codes, focusing on gates, measurements, and high-rate code constructions.
motivation: To extend fault-tolerant quantum error correction techniques from qubit systems to fermionic systems, specifically Majorana-based codes, which are promising for topological quantum computing.
method: Generalization of qubit fault-tolerant protocols to fermionic processes, including design of transversal gates, error correction procedures, and high-rate code constructions.
result: Creation of fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic systems, enabling gates and measurements in Majorana-based codes with improved rates.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana fermions, with implications for topological quantum computation and error correction.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits easier to simulate classically via Pauli propagation.
motivation: To understand the impact of noise on classical simulability of quantum circuits, which is important for benchmarking and error mitigation.
method: The authors develop a Pauli propagation method to simulate quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise, analyzing the computational cost.
result: Arbitrary local noise reduces the effective circuit depth, enabling efficient classical simulation of typical circuits.
conclusion: Noisy quantum circuits may lose quantum advantage; the method provides a tool for assessing classical simulability.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are introduced as a new class of low-density parity-check codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: To develop quantum error-correcting codes that are practical for near-term devices, balancing strong error correction with small size and tunable parameters.
method: The authors propose radial codes, a family of LDPC codes, and analyze their performance in terms of threshold, overhead, and single-shot decoding capability.
result: Radial codes achieve high error thresholds, low qubit overhead, and can be decoded in a single shot, making them promising for fault-tolerant quantum memory.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for near-term quantum devices, but further work is needed to assess their compatibility with specific hardware and to develop efficient decoders.

title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks Are Effectively Classically Simulable
authors: Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, and M. Cerezo

The action of a quantum convolutional neural network, which is a promising architecture for quantum machine learning, can be efficiently simulated by a classical computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020304] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: Quantum convolutional neural networks can be efficiently simulated classically, challenging their quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether quantum convolutional neural networks offer a computational advantage over classical methods.
method: The authors likely analyze the structure of QCNNs and prove that their action can be simulated efficiently on a classical computer, possibly using tensor network or other classical simulation techniques.
result: QCNNs are effectively classically simulable, meaning they do not provide a quantum advantage for the tasks considered.
conclusion: The findings suggest that QCNNs may not be a viable candidate for near-term quantum advantage, and alternative quantum machine learning architectures should be explored.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism since its experimental realization in 2016.
method: Review article summarizing experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, expanding theoretical understanding and opening new application directions.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on local energy, momentum, and spin densities.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles, a topic with applications in trapping, manipulation, and sorting.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical frameworks and experimental results from optics and acoustics, emphasizing a unified perspective based on local densities.
result: It covers applications such as optical trapping, acoustic sorting, and pulling forces, and highlights the role of spin and momentum densities.
conclusion: The review offers a unified understanding of radiation forces and torques, with implications for particle manipulation and future studies in wave-matter interactions.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics using brickwork quantum circuits, focusing on exactly solvable models.
motivation: To provide a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality and quantum circuit analogies can simplify the computation of quantum many-body dynamics.
method: Review of theoretical framework based on space-time duality in discrete lattice systems, with emphasis on brickwork quantum circuits.
result: Unified view of dynamical evolution in many-body systems via space-time duality, linking to quantum computation.
conclusion: The approach offers a powerful tool for studying quantum dynamics, but the paper is a review and does not present new results directly applicable to the user's specific interests.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: This review covers exotic electronic states in kagome metals, focusing on topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena observed in kagome metals, driven by frustrated geometry and strong correlations.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematicity.
conclusion: The review elucidates key mechanisms and suggests future directions for exploring correlated and topological physics in these materials.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: This pedagogical review applies field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems using field-theoretic methods, which are powerful but often scattered across different disciplines.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can unify various approaches to reaction-diffusion systems, offering a systematic way to handle fluctuations and correlations.
conclusion: The methods have broad applicability beyond chemistry, such as in ecology and epidemiology, and provide a foundation for further theoretical developments.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: This review updates the field of spin glasses, covering experiment, theory, and simulations, with emphasis on their synergy.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass dynamics and highlight the interplay between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of existing literature and synthesis of experimental, theoretical, and large-scale simulation results.
result: The paper tracks progress in spin-glass research and identifies future opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: This review covers theoretical and experimental progress on Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of Kitaev spin liquids, which are a paradigmatic example of quantum spin liquids with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials like α-RuCl3, discussing techniques such as neutron scattering and thermal transport.
result: Key findings include the identification of candidate materials, observation of fractionalized excitations, and chiral edge modes, confirming predictions of the Kitaev model.
conclusion: The review highlights open questions and future directions, such as realizing a true quantum spin liquid ground state and exploring device applications.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze large-scale neural recordings, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how coordinated neural activity in the brain can be described using principles from statistical physics.
method: Review of recent experiments recording electrical activity from thousands of neurons, analyzed with maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques.
result: Statistical physics models can quantitatively reproduce neural activity patterns and reveal reproducible behaviors.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience, similar to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: This review covers theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions relevant to photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of theoretical approaches describing internal conversion, a key photophysical process, and to guide applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper is a review that surveys various theoretical models for internal conversion, including quantum dynamics and rate theories.
result: The review summarizes the state of the art in modeling internal conversion and discusses how these models can be integrated into applied research.
conclusion: The authors suggest that improved theoretical methods can enhance the design of materials for photonics and energy harvesting, but the paper does not present new results.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of nonequilibrium dynamics in photoexcited Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and photoinduced phase transitions.
motivation: To understand and control material properties using light in strongly correlated systems, exploring novel optical responses and metastable phases.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders (superconducting, magnetic, orbital, excitonic) are highlighted.
conclusion: Provides a framework for future research in nonequilibrium strongly correlated systems, with potential for material control and quantum metastable phases.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including their formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of quantum properties of magnetic skyrmions, which have been studied mainly classically, and to highlight their potential for quantum technologies.
method: Review article summarizing theoretical and experimental progress on quantum skyrmions, covering topological aspects, quantum dynamics, and interactions.
result: Discusses quantum tunneling, superposition, and entanglement of skyrmions, as well as quantum effects in skyrmion formation.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new quantum technologies, but many open questions remain regarding their observation and control.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To systematically survey the landscape of spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons, which could reveal new physics beyond the Standard Model and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review that summarizes theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions (e.g., from axions, Z' bosons) and surveys experimental techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and spin-precession experiments.
result: The review catalogs numerous experimental constraints on spin-dependent couplings and discusses the implications for discrete symmetry violations and dark matter candidates.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, with many experimental bounds improving but no definitive detection yet; future experiments with increased sensitivity are needed.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to simplify multiqubit gate decompositions and realize quantum algorithms, with a focus on experimental implementations.
motivation: To survey the potential advantages of qudits over qubits in quantum computing, particularly for reducing circuit complexity and resource requirements.
method: The paper provides a review of theoretical proposals and experimental demonstrations of qudit-based quantum computing, including qudit-qubit embeddings and gate decompositions.
result: Qudits can simplify certain multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate) and reduce the number of operations, but practical challenges remain in qudit control and coherence.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising alternative for quantum computing, but further experimental progress is needed to realize their full potential.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on physical properties due to violations of underlying assumptions in measurement contexts.
motivation: To clarify why some measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to explore how materials can be designed to violate these assumptions for enhanced properties.
method: A review of various experimental and theoretical cases where measured properties exceed classical bounds, analyzing which assumptions are violated.
result: Many apparent violations arise from non-equilibrium conditions, inhomogeneities, or other deviations from the assumptions of classical thermodynamics.
conclusion: Understanding these violations can lead to the development of materials with superior properties, but the findings do not challenge fundamental thermodynamics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data up to the end of 2022.
motivation: To provide an updated, self-consistent set of fundamental constants for use in science and technology, reflecting the latest experimental and theoretical improvements.
method: A least-squares adjustment that combines data from various experiments and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties.
result: A new set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors, with improved precision compared to previous adjustments.
conclusion: The updated constants are essential for accurate measurements and theoretical calculations across physics and chemistry, and the methodology continues to evolve with new data.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the current ability to predict spin coherence times using ab initio methods, which is crucial for quantum technologies.
method: Review of cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, with discussion of higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion methods yield reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations and decoherence from surfaces/interfaces.
conclusion: The field is maturing, with predictive capabilities improving, but further development is needed to handle complex decoherence mechanisms.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries

We determine the magnetic ground state of the kagome lattice magnet [MATH] by single-crystal neutron diffraction, supported by experiments with polarized neutrons. We identify this material as a collinear ferromagnet (“hex-FM”) with uniform moment leng…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper determines the magnetic ground state of the kagome magnet Nd3Ru4Al12 as a collinear ferromagnet with reduced moment length using neutron diffraction.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of kagome lattice materials, which are of interest for frustrated magnetism and topological phases.
method: Single-crystal neutron diffraction and polarized neutron experiments.
result: The material is a collinear ferromagnet (hex-FM) with uniform but reduced magnetic moment length.
conclusion: Provides insight into the magnetic ordering of kagome magnets, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ultrafast Structural Dynamics Of SnSe Under Photoexcitation Uncovered By Real-time Time-dependent Density Functional Theory Calculations
authors: Luoyao Yang, Liyuan Chen (陈丽媛), Hongli Chen (陈红丽), Liyan Shang (商丽燕), Yawei Li (李亚巍), Liangqing Zhu (朱亮清), Jinzhong Zhang (张金中), Shijing Gong (龚士静), And Zhigao Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Luoyao Yang, Liyuan Chen (陈丽媛), Hongli Chen (陈红丽), Liyan Shang (商丽燕), Yawei Li (李亚巍), Liangqing Zhu (朱亮清), Jinzhong Zhang (张金中), Shijing Gong (龚士静), and Zhigao Hu (胡志高)

Recently, a high-efficiency thermoelectric candidate SnSe has been experimentally shown to undergo a phase transition induced by femtosecond laser excitation, but the underlying microscopic mechanism has not been fully clarified. Photoinduced phase transitions provide an effective means to disentang…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224104] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses real-time time-dependent density functional theory to study ultrafast structural dynamics and photoinduced phase transition in SnSe, a thermoelectric material.
motivation: To clarify the microscopic mechanism of femtosecond laser-induced phase transition in SnSe, which is important for understanding and controlling material properties.
method: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory (rt-TDDFT) calculations.
result: The study uncovers the ultrafast structural dynamics and the pathway of the photoinduced phase transition in SnSe.
conclusion: Provides insights into photoinduced phase transitions, which may aid in designing materials with tailored properties, but is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Interface-driven Enhancement Of Magnetic Anisotropy In Infinite-layer Cuprate/manganite Heterostructures
authors: Digbijaya Palai, B. Samantaray, Poonam Sharma, D. Sahoo, Kishori Lal, S. Kale, G. Tripathy, R. Soni, Nirmal Ganguli, Z. Hossain, And D. Samal
abstract:
Author(s): Digbijaya Palai, B. Samantaray, Poonam Sharma, D. Sahoo, Kishori Lal, S. Kale, G. Tripathy, R. Soni, Nirmal Ganguli, Z. Hossain, and D. Samal

Interfacial symmetry breaking leading to the preferential orbital occupation in complex oxide heterostructures offer effective routes to tailor magnetic anisotropy. We demonstrate the modulation of magnetic anisotropy in [MATH] (LSMO) thin films in…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic anisotropy in cuprate/manganite heterostructures, focusing on interface-driven orbital occupation effects.
motivation: To understand and control magnetic anisotropy in complex oxide heterostructures for potential spintronic applications.
method: Experimental growth and characterization of LSMO thin films on cuprate substrates, with theoretical modeling of orbital occupation.
result: Interface symmetry breaking leads to preferential orbital occupation, enhancing magnetic anisotropy.
conclusion: Provides a route to tailor magnetic anisotropy in oxide heterostructures, relevant for spintronics.

title: Exchange-dominated Frequency Shift Of The Spin-wave Nonreciprocal Dispersion Relation In Planar Magnetic Multilayers
authors: Claudia Negrete, Jorge A. Otálora, And Attila Kákay
abstract:
Author(s): Claudia Negrete, Jorge A. Otálora, and Attila Kákay

Spin-wave nonreciprocity, manifested as a frequency difference between counterpropagating modes, underpins many proposed magnonic devices. While this effect is commonly attributed to dipolar interactions or interfacial chirality, the microscopic origin of the frequency shift in nonreciprocal dispers…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224411] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the frequency shift in nonreciprocal spin-wave dispersion in planar magnetic multilayers, attributing it to exchange interactions rather than dipolar or interfacial effects.
motivation: To understand the microscopic origin of spin-wave nonreciprocity, which is important for magnonic devices but often attributed to dipolar or chiral effects.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of spin-wave dispersion in planar magnetic multilayers, focusing on exchange-dominated contributions.
result: The exchange interaction can cause a frequency shift between counterpropagating spin waves, leading to nonreciprocity even without dipolar or interfacial chirality.
conclusion: Exchange-dominated nonreciprocity provides a new mechanism for controlling spin waves in magnonic devices, with potential implications for information processing.

title: Computational Prediction Of Ferromagnetic ${at}_{6}{x}_{6}$ Kagome Compounds
authors: Shiya Chen, Zhen Zhang, Vladimir Antropov, And Yang Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Shiya Chen, Zhen Zhang, Vladimir Antropov, and Yang Sun

We present a systematic high-throughput density-functional-theory investigation of the structural and magnetic stability of 312 substitutional compounds in the magnetic kagome [MATH] family. Our screening confirms the stability of many previously reported structures and predicts several a…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224412] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A high-throughput DFT study predicting stable ferromagnetic kagome compounds in the AT6X6 family.
motivation: To discover new magnetic kagome materials for potential applications in spintronics and quantum phenomena.
method: High-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations screening 312 substitutional compounds for structural and magnetic stability.
result: Confirmed stability of known structures and predicted several new stable ferromagnetic kagome compounds.
conclusion: Provides a database of candidate materials for experimental synthesis and further study of kagome magnetism.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives exact upper bounds on the critical temperature for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations, based solely on the largest coordination number.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for a wide class of 2D lattices, which are useful for understanding phase transitions in statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical derivation using combinatorial and graph-theoretic arguments on periodic tessellations of the plane.
result: Exact upper bounds for the critical temperature expressed in terms of the maximum coordination number of the lattice.
conclusion: The bounds are universal and apply to any 2D periodic lattice, offering a simple tool to estimate critical temperatures without detailed calculations.

title: Diffusion-driven Pattern Formation In An Opinion Dynamical Network Model
authors: Tim Mauch And Thilo Gross
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Mauch and Thilo Gross

The spatial organization of individuals and their interactions in communities are important factors known to preserve diversity in many complex systems. Inspired by metapopulation models from ecology, we study opinion formation using a network-based approach in which nodes represent communities of i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion formation using a network model inspired by metapopulation ecology, focusing on spatial organization and diversity.
motivation: To understand how spatial organization and interactions in communities preserve diversity in opinion dynamics.
method: A network-based metapopulation model where nodes represent communities of individuals, with diffusion-driven pattern formation.
result: The model shows that spatial structure can lead to pattern formation and maintain diversity in opinions.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of spatial organization in opinion dynamics, with potential applications to social systems.

title: Free-energy Model Of Ferroelectric Transition In P(VDF-TrFE) Copolymer
authors: Vadim V. Atrazhev, Dmitry V. Dmitriev, And Vadim I. Sultanov
abstract:
Author(s): Vadim V. Atrazhev, Dmitry V. Dmitriev, and Vadim I. Sultanov

We develop a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in poly(vinylidene difluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) [P(VDF-TrFE)] copolymers. The low-temperature ferroelectric phase is an orthorhombic crystal analogous to the poly(vinylidene difluoride) β-phase, wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065405] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a free-energy model for the ferroelectric phase transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers, focusing on material physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand and predict the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric transition in a technologically important polymer for applications like sensors and actuators.
method: Physics-based analytical modeling using Landau-type free-energy expansion with parameters fitted to experimental data.
result: The model reproduces the transition temperature and polarization behavior, providing insights into the role of copolymer composition.
conclusion: The model can guide material design but has no direct connection to quantum computing, information thermodynamics, or quantum communication.

title: Virtual Cathode Behavior In A Crossed-field Gap
authors: Ashmita Panda, Jim Browning, And Allen L. Garner
abstract:
Author(s): Ashmita Panda, Jim Browning, and Allen L. Garner

While the behavior of virtual cathodes (VCs) in a space-charge limited gap in the absence of a magnetic field is well understood, it is less characterized for crossed-field gaps with perpendicular magnetic and electric fields. Thus, this study examines VC formation at steady state in a crossed-field…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065202] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies virtual cathode formation in crossed-field gaps, which is a topic in plasma physics and vacuum electronics, not directly related to the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand virtual cathode behavior in crossed-field gaps, which is less characterized than in magnetic-field-free gaps.
method: The study uses theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to examine steady-state VC formation under perpendicular magnetic and electric fields.
result: Key findings likely include conditions for VC formation and its characteristics in crossed-field gaps.
conclusion: The results may inform design of crossed-field devices, but no direct implications for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nonlinear Dynamics Of Slow Ions Near The Cyclotron Resonance: A Possibility For Optimization Of An Electrodeless Plasma Thruster
authors: Maxim Tereshchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Maxim Tereshchenko

The cyclotron resonance dynamics of ions in a uniform magnetic field under the action of a plane left-handed polarized wave is considered. The dynamics of initially slow ions is nonlinear: they periodically synchronously (regardless of the initial phase of interaction) gain and then lose energy. The…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065203] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear cyclotron resonance dynamics of slow ions in a magnetic field for optimizing electrodeless plasma thrusters.
motivation: To understand and optimize the energy transfer from a left-handed polarized wave to ions in a plasma thruster, which is relevant for spacecraft propulsion.
method: Theoretical analysis of ion dynamics under cyclotron resonance using a plane left-handed polarized wave, considering nonlinear effects and initial phase independence.
result: Ions periodically synchronously gain and lose energy regardless of initial phase, indicating a nonlinear energy exchange mechanism.
conclusion: The findings may enable optimization of electrodeless plasma thrusters by exploiting the nonlinear dynamics for more efficient ion acceleration.

title: Water In Motion: How Charged Semiflexible Nanofibers Affect Self-diffusion Of Water
authors: Hanno Holzinger, Ahmad Reza Motezakker, Sergey V. Dvinskikh, Korneliya Gordeyeva, Per Tomas Larsson, And Daniel Söderberg
abstract:
Author(s): Hanno Holzinger, Ahmad Reza Motezakker, Sergey V. Dvinskikh, Korneliya Gordeyeva, Per Tomas Larsson, and Daniel Söderberg

Even at very low concentrations, the rheology of dispersions of charged semiflexible nanofibers differs from the rheology of the pure liquid, given the fiber charge, morphology, and interactions. At the nanoscale, the thermal motion of fibers is driven by the collective motion of the solvent molecul…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065403] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how charged semiflexible nanofibers affect water self-diffusion, focusing on rheology and nanoscale dynamics.
motivation: To understand how low concentrations of charged nanofibers alter the rheological properties of water, which is important for applications in materials science and biology.
method: Experimental techniques (likely NMR or scattering) to measure self-diffusion of water in dispersions of charged semiflexible nanofibers.
result: The presence of charged nanofibers modifies water self-diffusion even at very low concentrations, due to fiber charge and morphology.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into nanoscale solvent dynamics in complex fluids, with implications for designing nanofiber-based materials.

title: First-passage-time Properties Of Diffusion With A Broad Class Of Stochastic Diffusion Coefficients
authors: Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, And Hitoshi Washizu
abstract:
Author(s): Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, and Hitoshi Washizu

This study investigates the first-passage-time (FPT) properties of particles with a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients (DCs), representing diffusion in heterogeneous environments or of particles with conformational fluctuations. We demonstrate that for diffusion in a one-dimen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064108] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage-time properties of diffusion with stochastic diffusion coefficients in one dimension.
motivation: To understand diffusion in heterogeneous environments or of particles with conformational fluctuations, where the diffusion coefficient itself fluctuates stochastically.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of first-passage-time statistics for a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients in one-dimensional diffusion.
result: The paper derives general properties of first-passage times, showing how stochasticity in the diffusion coefficient affects the distribution and moments of first-passage times.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transport in disordered media and may inform models of stochastic processes in physics and biology.

title: Relative-advection-induced Instability In A Reaction-diffusion-advection System
authors: Chuanjun Dai, Ruyi Zhou, Qing Guo, And Min Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Chuanjun Dai, Ruyi Zhou, Qing Guo, and Min Zhao

The instability mechanism in general reaction-diffusion-advection systems is key to understanding flow-driven self-organization. Here we report the general conditions for instability in [MATH]-dimensional space, formally termed relative advection instability (RAI) given its exclusive dependence on the …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064202] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies instability in reaction-diffusion-advection systems, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand flow-driven self-organization in classical reaction-diffusion-advection systems.
method: Theoretical analysis of general conditions for instability in n-dimensional space, focusing on relative advection.
result: Identified a new instability mechanism called relative advection instability (RAI) that depends solely on advection differences.
conclusion: Provides general conditions for pattern formation in advective systems, with implications for ecology and fluid dynamics.

title: Resetting-induced Instability In Queues Fed By A Search Process In An Interval
authors: José Giral-Barajas And Paul C. Bressloff
abstract:
Author(s): José Giral-Barajas and Paul C. Bressloff

Proper management of resources whose arrival and consumption are subject to environmental randomness is an intrinsic process in both natural and artificial systems. This phenomenon can be modeled as a queuing process whose arrival distribution is determined by a search process with stochastic resett…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064101] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies instability in queues where arrivals are governed by a search process with stochastic resetting, a topic in statistical physics and queueing theory.
motivation: To understand how resetting events in a search process affect the stability of a queue, which has implications for resource management in natural and artificial systems.
method: The authors model the arrival process as a search with stochastic resetting in an interval and analyze the queue length distribution and stability conditions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that resetting can induce instability in the queue, leading to diverging mean queue lengths under certain conditions, and characterize the phase transition between stable and unstable regimes.
conclusion: The work highlights the impact of resetting on queue dynamics and suggests future studies on more complex resetting protocols or service disciplines.

title: Quantum Size Effect And Two-step Condensation Of Ideal Bose Atoms In An Optical Hard-wall Nanotube
authors: Ze Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Ze Cheng

We consider a quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) system that is an optical hard-wall nanotube with axial harmonic potential. This quasi-1D system possesses a quasi-1D harmonic potential that consists of a 1D harmonic trap along the [MATH] axis and a two-dimensional box trap in the [MATH] plane. Wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064106] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Bose-Einstein condensation in a quasi-1D optical nanotube with hard-wall and harmonic confinement, focusing on quantum size effects and two-step condensation.
motivation: To understand how quantum confinement in quasi-1D geometries affects Bose-Einstein condensation, particularly the role of hard-wall boundaries and harmonic traps.
method: Theoretical analysis using ideal Bose gas model in a quasi-1D harmonic potential with a 2D box trap, solving the grand canonical ensemble and computing condensation temperatures.
result: Predicts a two-step condensation process and quantum size effects due to the discrete energy levels in the transverse direction.
conclusion: Provides insights into low-dimensional Bose condensation, but the system is idealized and may not directly apply to experimental realizations.

title: Relaxation Of The Random Site Coulomb Glass Model In Two Dimensions
authors: Preeti Bhandari And Vikas Malik
abstract:
Author(s): Preeti Bhandari and Vikas Malik

This study investigates the influence of material density, disorder in onsite energies, and localization length on relaxation dynamics within a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model at half-filling. To explore relaxation laws, we calculate the eigenvalue distribution of the linear dynamica…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064107] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies relaxation dynamics in a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model, focusing on the influence of disorder and localization length.
motivation: To understand how material density, disorder, and localization length affect relaxation in disordered electronic systems, which is relevant for glassy dynamics and transport.
method: Numerical calculation of eigenvalue distributions of the linear dynamics matrix for the random site Coulomb glass model at half-filling.
result: The relaxation laws depend on density, disorder strength, and localization length, with specific eigenvalue distributions characterizing the dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into relaxation in disordered systems, but the paper is not directly connected to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Competition Between Private And Expressed Opinions In Binary Choice: The $α\text{−}\mathrm{EPO}$ $q$-voter Model
authors: Barbara Kamińska, Barbara Nowak, Arkadiusz Lipiecki, And Katarzyna Sznajd-Weron
abstract:
Author(s): Barbara Kamińska, Barbara Nowak, Arkadiusz Lipiecki, and Katarzyna Sznajd-Weron

People often express opinions that differ from their privately held views, a phenomenon known in economy as preference falsification. Expressed-private opinion (EPO) models capture this by assigning each agent two dynamical variables: a private (internal) and an expressed (external) opinion. Within …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a sociophysics model of opinion dynamics where agents have both private and expressed opinions, focusing on the competition between them in binary choices.
motivation: To understand the phenomenon of preference falsification, where individuals publicly express opinions that differ from their private beliefs, using a statistical physics approach.
method: The authors introduce the α-EPO q-voter model, an extension of the q-voter model, where each agent has two binary variables (private and expressed opinion) and update rules based on social influence and conformity.
result: The model exhibits various phases including consensus, polarization, and a 'private opinion dominance' phase, depending on parameters like the fraction of conformists and the number of influencing neighbors.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how social pressure can lead to a gap between private and expressed opinions, with potential applications in understanding public opinion dynamics and social phenomena.

title: Learning Stochastic Cellular Dynamics From Snapshots Through Bidirectional Causal Neural Stochastic Differential Equations
authors: Yuting Meng, Rabia Sultan, Peixuan Jiang, Qiuman Wang, Dian Tan, Jiao Wang, Peiluan Li, And Luonan Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuting Meng, Rabia Sultan, Peixuan Jiang, Qiuman Wang, Dian Tan, Jiao Wang, Peiluan Li, and Luonan Chen

Due to cell destruction in sequencing, time-series data yield unpaired snapshots, obscuring lineages and gene dynamics in individual cells. Current data-driven methods rely on single-variate expression, ignoring cell types and rotational effects in nonsteady states, limiting interpretability and acc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a causal neural SDE framework to infer stochastic cellular dynamics from unpaired snapshot data, focusing on gene regulatory networks and cell differentiation.
motivation: Time-series single-cell sequencing destroys cells, yielding unpaired snapshots that obscure lineage and gene dynamics; existing methods ignore cell types and rotational effects in nonsteady states.
method: The authors propose a bidirectional causal neural stochastic differential equation (SDE) model that learns latent dynamics from snapshot data by incorporating causal structures and handling nonsteady-state rotational effects.
result: The model successfully reconstructs continuous cell trajectories and gene regulatory interactions from unpaired snapshots, outperforming existing methods on synthetic and real datasets.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for inferring cellular dynamics from destructive measurements, with potential applications in developmental biology and disease modeling.

title: Intrinsic Noise Suppression In Protein Allostery: Quantifying Pathway Redundancy Via Spanning Tree Statistics
authors: Burak Erman
abstract:
Author(s): Burak Erman

Allosteric regulation in proteins arises from collective dynamics distributed over networks of residue contacts, but how multiple communication pathways contribute to signal transmission and noise suppression remains unclear. Here we develop a spanning-tree-based framework to quantify allosteric com…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spanning-tree-based framework to quantify allosteric communication pathways and noise suppression in proteins, which is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand how multiple communication pathways in protein allostery contribute to signal transmission and noise suppression.
method: Spanning-tree-based statistical framework to analyze residue contact networks.
result: Quantified pathway redundancy and its role in intrinsic noise suppression.
conclusion: Provides insights into allosteric regulation but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Oscillatory Evolutionarily Stable State And Limit Cycle In Replicator Dynamics
authors: Suman Chakraborty, Vikash Kumar Dubey, Vaibhav Madhok, And Sagar Chakraborty
abstract:
Author(s): Suman Chakraborty, Vikash Kumar Dubey, Vaibhav Madhok, and Sagar Chakraborty

The idea of the evolutionarily stable state (ESS) of a population is a cornerstone of evolutionary game theory; moreover, it coincides with the game-theoretic concept of Nash equilibrium. Such a state corresponds to a strategy adopted by the population such that a rare mutant strategy cannot invade …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062201] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillatory evolutionarily stable states and limit cycles in replicator dynamics from evolutionary game theory.
motivation: To extend the concept of evolutionarily stable states to non-equilibrium oscillatory behaviors in population dynamics.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of replicator dynamics models, focusing on conditions for oscillatory ESS and limit cycles.
result: Identified conditions under which oscillatory states can be evolutionarily stable, and characterized limit cycle attractors.
conclusion: Provides a framework for understanding cyclic evolutionary strategies, with potential applications in biology and social sciences.

title: Order-disorder Transition In Incompressible Polar Active Fluids With An Easy Axis
authors: Leiming Chen, Chiu Fan Lee, And John Toner
abstract:
Author(s): Leiming Chen, Chiu Fan Lee, and John Toner

Dry active matter in an anisotropic medium is of experimental relevance, and the interplay between anisotropy and the dynamics of the active matter remains under-explored. Here, we derive the hydrodynamic equations of a generic dry polar active fluid that preferentially flows along a particular axis…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054142] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the order-disorder transition in dry polar active fluids with an easy axis, focusing on anisotropic effects in active matter.
motivation: To understand how anisotropy influences the dynamics and phase transitions of dry polar active fluids, which is relevant for experimental systems in anisotropic media.
method: The authors derive hydrodynamic equations for a generic dry polar active fluid that preferentially flows along a particular axis, and analyze the resulting phase behavior.
result: They find that the easy axis leads to a rich phase diagram with order-disorder transitions, and characterize the critical properties.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for anisotropic active matter, with implications for experimental realizations and further studies of nonequilibrium phase transitions.

title: Wave Breaking And Electron Heating Of Perpendicularly Propagating $x$-mode Waves In Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Jin-Ze Liu, Heng Zhang, Dong-Ning Gao, And Wen-Shan Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Jin-Ze Liu, Heng Zhang, Dong-Ning Gao, and Wen-Shan Duan

This study uses three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations to investigate the nonlinear evolution of electromagnetic waves propagating perpendicular to an external magnetic field in a magnetized plasma, with an emphasis on wave breaking and electron energization. In the weakly nonlinear regime (…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 055214] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave breaking and electron heating of x-mode waves in magnetized plasmas using particle-in-cell simulations.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave evolution and electron energization in magnetized plasmas, relevant to space and fusion plasmas.
method: Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of electromagnetic waves propagating perpendicular to an external magnetic field.
result: Wave breaking and electron heating occur in the weakly nonlinear regime for x-mode waves.
conclusion: Provides insights into plasma heating mechanisms but has no direct connection to quantum information or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Collective Dynamics Of Macroscopic Photoactive Matter Under Alternating Excitation Patterns
authors: Sára Lévay, Axel Katona, Raúl Cruz Hidalgo, And Iker Zuriguel
abstract:
Author(s): Sára Lévay, Axel Katona, Raúl Cruz Hidalgo, and Iker Zuriguel

We present experiments on the collective dynamics of macroscopic photoactive self-propelled particles subjected to spatiotemporally varying excitation. The particles move within an arena divided into two regions with different illumination intensities, creating alternating bright (more active) and d…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 055423] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics of macroscopic photoactive particles under alternating light patterns, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how spatiotemporal excitation patterns affect the collective motion of active particles.
method: Experiments with photoactive self-propelled particles in an arena with alternating bright and dark regions.
result: The particles exhibit collective dynamics influenced by the alternating excitation patterns.
conclusion: The findings contribute to active matter physics but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Describing A Universal Critical Behavior In A Transition From Order To Chaos
authors: Edson D. Leonel, Mayla A. M. de Almeida, Juan Pedro Tarigo, Arturo C. Marti, And Diego F. M. Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Edson D. Leonel, Mayla A. M. de Almeida, Juan Pedro Tarigo, Arturo C. Marti, and Diego F. M. Oliveira

We present a comprehensive discussion of a transition from integrability to nonintegrability in an oval billiard with a static boundary. This transition is controlled by a deformation parameter [MATH], which modifies the boundary shape from circular, corresponding to [MATH] and an integrable dynamics, t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054220] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transition from integrability to nonintegrability in an oval billiard system, focusing on universal critical behavior in order-to-chaos transitions.
motivation: To understand the universal aspects of the transition from integrable to chaotic dynamics in Hamiltonian systems, using a billiard model with a tunable deformation parameter.
method: Numerical simulations and analytical scaling analysis of an oval billiard with a static boundary, varying a deformation parameter to control the transition.
result: Identified universal critical exponents and scaling laws characterizing the transition from order to chaos.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the universality of chaos transitions in classical Hamiltonian systems, with potential extensions to other nonlinear systems.

title: Emergent Domain Segregation In Self-interacting Polymers Explains Chromosome 3d Conformations In Single Human Cells
authors: Mattia Conte, Simona Bianco, Sougata Guha, Andrea M. Chiariello, Andrea Esposito, Alex Abraham, Sumanta Kundu, Francesca Vercellone, Andrea Fontana, Florinda Di Pierno, Ciro Di Carluccio, Matteo Olimpo, And Mario Nicodemi
abstract:
Author(s): Mattia Conte, Simona Bianco, Sougata Guha, Andrea M. Chiariello, Andrea Esposito, Alex Abraham, Sumanta Kundu, Francesca Vercellone, Andrea Fontana, Florinda Di Pierno, Ciro Di Carluccio, Matteo Olimpo, and Mario Nicodemi

Polymer physics models have been employed to elucidate the 3D organization of chromosomes in the cell nucleus. However, how well they capture chromatin architectures at the single-molecule level remains poorly understood. Here, we consider a minimal polymer model where folding is driven by sequence-…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054416] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a minimal polymer model to study chromosome 3D organization in single cells, focusing on domain segregation driven by self-interactions.
motivation: To understand how well polymer physics models capture chromatin architecture at the single-molecule level, which is poorly understood.
method: A minimal polymer model with sequence-dependent interactions is used to simulate chromosome folding and compare with single-cell Hi-C data.
result: The model reproduces emergent domain segregation and key features of chromosome 3D conformations observed in single human cells.
conclusion: The findings validate the polymer model for single-cell chromatin organization and suggest that simple physical principles can explain complex genome architecture.

title: Time Delay In The One-dimensional Swarmalator Model
authors: K. P. O'keeffe, Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, And Jason Hindes
abstract:
Author(s): K. P. O'Keeffe, Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, and Jason Hindes

We study the one-dimensional (1D) swarmalator model with time-delayed interactions. Delay preserves the familiar static states—sync, async, and phase wave—but generates two new families of nonstatic states. One bifurcates from the phase wave at [MATH]; the other bifurcates from the async s…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054219] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-delayed interactions in the 1D swarmalator model, revealing new nonstatic states.
motivation: To understand how time delay affects collective behavior in swarmalator systems, which model swarming and synchronization.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the 1D swarmalator model with time-delayed coupling.
result: Time delay preserves static states but introduces two new families of nonstatic states bifurcating from phase wave and async states.
conclusion: Time delay enriches the dynamics of swarmalator models, with implications for biological and robotic swarms.

title: Phenomenology Of Orbital Torque, Pumping, And Mixing Conductance In Metallic Bilayers
authors: Xiaobai Ning, Henri Jaffrès, Weisheng Zhao, And Aurélien Manchon
abstract:

The conversion between spin and orbital currents is at the origin of the orbital torque and its Onsager reciprocal, the orbital pumping. Here, we propose a phenomenological model to describe the orbital torque in magnetic bilayers composed of an orbital source (i.e., a light metal such as Ti, Ru, ${…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023239] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phenomenological model for orbital torque and pumping in metallic bilayers, focusing on spin-orbit conversion in light metals.
motivation: To understand the conversion between spin and orbital currents in magnetic bilayers, which is key for orbital torque and its reciprocal effect.
method: A phenomenological model is proposed to describe orbital torque in bilayers composed of an orbital source (light metal) and a ferromagnet.
result: The model captures the orbital torque and pumping, and defines mixing conductance for orbital currents.
conclusion: Provides a framework for interpreting experiments on orbital torque and may guide future spintronic devices.
